p3.original: If you were born within the last three decades in the United States, Canada, or many other countries in the developed world, you probably have no real experience with a high rate of inflation. Inflation is when most prices in an entire economy are rising. However, there is an extreme form of inflation called hyperinflation. This occurred in Germany between 1921 and 1928, and more recently in Zimbabwe between 2008 and 2009. In November 2008, Zimbabwe had an inflation rate of 79.6 billion percent. In contrast, in 2014, the United States had an average annual rate of inflation of 1.6%.
p3.zh: 如果你出生于美国,加拿大,或者发达世界的很多其他国家 在过去三十年里,你可能没有 高通胀率的真正经验。通货膨胀是整个经济中大多数价格上升的时候。 然而,有一种极端形式的通货膨胀,称为恶性通货膨胀。 这发生在1921年至1928年间的德国,最近发生在2008年至2009年间的津巴布韦.2008年11月,津巴布韦的通货膨胀率为796亿。相比之下,2014年美国年平均通货膨胀率为1.6%.

p4.original: Zimbabwe’s inflation rate was so high it is difficult to comprehend, so let’s put it into context. It is equivalent to price increases of 98% per day. This means that, from one day to the next, prices essentially double. What is life like in an economy afflicted with hyperinflation? Most of you reading this will have never experienced this phenomenon. The government adjusted prices for commodities in Zimbabwean dollars several times each day. There was no desire to hold on to currency since it lost value by the minute. The people there spent a great deal of time getting rid of any cash they acquired by purchasing whatever food or other commodities they could find. At one point, a loaf of bread cost 550 million Zimbabwean dollars. Teachers' salaries were in the trillions a month; however, this was equivalent to only one U.S. dollar a day. At its height, it took 621,984,228 Zimbabwean dollars to purchase one U.S. dollar.
p4.zh: 津巴布韦的通胀率如此之高,很难理解,所以让我们把它放在背景上。相当于每天涨价98%。 这意味着,从一天到第二天,价格基本上翻了一番。在一个饱受恶性通货膨胀困扰的经济中,生活是什么样子? 你们大多数人读到这本书时 从来没有经历过这个现象。 政府每天数次调整以津巴布韦元计的商品价格。 由于货币在一分钟之内就失去价值,所以没有保持货币的意愿。那里的人们花了很多时间来摆脱他们通过购买他们能找到的任何食物或其他商品而获得的任何现金. 一连串面包 耗资5.5亿津巴布韦元。教师的工资是每月数万亿美元;然而,这相当于每天只有一美元。其鼎盛时期,津巴布韦花费621,984,228美元购买了1美元.

p5.original: Government agencies had no money to pay their workers so they started printing money to pay their bills rather than raising taxes. Rising prices caused the government to enact price controls on private businesses, which led to shortages and the emergence of black markets. In 2009, the country abandoned its currency and allowed people to use foreign currencies for purchases.
p5.zh: 政府机构没有钱支付工人工资,因此它们开始印刷钱来支付账单,而不是提高税收。价格上涨导致政府对私营企业实行价格控制,导致短缺和黑市的出现.2009年,该国放弃货币,允许人们使用外币购买.

p6.original: How does this happen? How can both government and the economy fail to function at the most basic level? Before we consider these extreme cases of hyperinflation, let’s first look at inflation itself.
p6.zh: 怎么会这样?政府和经济体如何不能在最基本的层面上运作? 在考虑这些恶性通货膨胀的极端情况之前,让我们先看看通货膨胀本身。

p11.original: How the U.S. and Other Countries Experience Inflation
p11.zh: 美国和其他国家是如何经历通货膨胀的

p14.original: Inflation is a general and ongoing rise in the level of prices in an entire economy. Inflation does not refer to a change in relative prices. A relative price change occurs when you see that the price of tuition has risen, but the price of laptops has fallen. Inflation, on the other hand, means that there is pressure for prices to rise in most markets in the economy. In addition, price increases in the supply-and-demand model were one-time events, representing a shift from a previous equilibrium to a new one. Inflation implies an ongoing rise in prices. If inflation happened for one year and then stopped, then it would not be inflation any more.
p14.zh: 通货膨胀是整个经济中价格水平的普遍和持续上升。通货膨胀不是指相对价格的变动. 当看到学费价格上涨,但笔记本电脑价格下跌时,价格就发生了相对变化. 另一方面,通货膨胀意味着经济中大多数市场的价格都有上升的压力。 此外,供求模式中的价格上涨是一次性事件,表明从以前的平衡转向新的平衡。通货膨胀意味着物价持续上涨。 如果通货膨胀发生一年,然后停止,那就不再是通货膨胀了。

p15.original: This chapter begins by showing how to combine prices of individual goods and services to create a measure of overall inflation. It discusses the historical and recent experience of inflation, both in the United States and in other countries around the world. Other chapters have sometimes included a note under an exhibit or a parenthetical reminder in the text saying that the numbers have been adjusted for inflation. In this chapter, it is time to show how to use inflation statistics to adjust other economic variables, so that you can tell how much of, for example, we can attribute the rise in GDP over different periods of time to an actual increase in the production of goods and services and how much we should attribute to the fact that prices for most items have risen.
p15.zh: 本章首先说明如何将个别货物和服务的价格结合起来,以形成一个衡量总体通货膨胀的尺度。 它讨论了美国和世界其他国家历史上和最近通货膨胀的经验。 其他章节有时在展品下加注,或在案文中加括号提醒,说明数字已根据通货膨胀作出调整。 在本章中,现在应该说明如何使用通货膨胀统计来调整其他经济变量,以便你能够知道,例如,我们可以把不同时期国内生产总值的上升归因于商品和服务生产的实际增长,以及我们应该把多少归因于大多数项目的价格已经上涨这一事实。

p16.original: Inflation has consequences for people and firms throughout the economy, in their roles as lenders and borrowers, wage-earners, taxpayers, and consumers. The chapter concludes with a discussion of some imperfections and biases in the inflation statistics, and a preview of policies for fighting inflation that we will discuss in other chapters.
p16.zh: 通货膨胀对整个经济中的人和公司产生影响,因为他们是贷款人和借款人、挣工资者、纳税人和消费者。本章最后讨论了通货膨胀统计中的一些不完善和偏颇之处,并介绍了我们将在其他章节中讨论的遏制通货膨胀的政策。

p18.original: Dinner table conversations where you might have heard about inflation usually entail reminiscing about when “everything seemed to cost so much less. You used to be able to buy three gallons of gasoline for a dollar and then go see an afternoon movie for another dollar.”  compares some prices of common goods in 1970 and 2017. Of course, the average prices in this table may not reflect the prices where you live. The cost of living in New York City is much higher than in Houston, Texas, for example. In addition, certain products have evolved over recent decades. A new car in 2021, loaded with antipollution equipment, safety gear, computerized engine controls, and many other technological advances, is a more advanced machine (and more fuel efficient) than your typical 1970s car. However, put details like these to one side for the moment, and look at the overall pattern. The primary reason behind the price rises in —and all the price increases for the other products in the economy—is not specific to the market for housing or cars or gasoline or movie tickets. Instead, it is part of a general rise in the level of all prices. At the beginning of 2021, $1 had about the same purchasing power in overall terms of goods and services as 15 cents did in 1972, because of the amount of inflation that has occurred over that time period.
p18.zh: 你可能听说过通货膨胀的餐桌对话通常意味着要回忆“每件事似乎都要花费少得多的时间。 你过去可以买三加仑汽油换一美元,然后去看另一美元的下午电影。” 比较了1970年和2017年的一些普通商品价格。 当然,本表中的平均价格可能不能反映你所生活的价格. 例如,纽约市的生活费用远高于德克萨斯州休斯敦。 此外,最近几十年中,某些产品有所发展。2021年的一款新车,装有防污染设备,安全齿轮,计算机化发动机控制装置,以及许多其他技术进步,是比您典型的1970年代车型更先进的机器(和燃料效率更高). 然而,现在把这样的细节放在一边,看看总体模式.价格上涨的主要原因——以及经济中其他产品价格的所有上涨——并非住房、汽车、汽油或电影票市场所特有的。 相反,它是所有价格水平普遍上升的一部分。2021年初,1美元在货物和服务整体购买力上与1972年的15美分相同,因为这一时期发生的通货膨胀幅度很大.

p48.original: A modern economy has millions of goods and services whose prices are continually quivering in the breezes of supply and demand. How can all of these shifts in price attribute to a single inflation rate? As with many problems in economic measurement, the conceptual answer is reasonably straightforward: Economists combine prices of a variety of goods and services into a single price level. The inflation rate is simply the percentage change in the price level. Applying the concept, however, involves some practical difficulties.
p48.zh: 现代经济有数百万个货物和服务,其价格在供求微风中不断波动。 所有这些价格属性如何能改变为单一通货膨胀率?与经济计量的许多问题一样,概念答案也是相当直截了当的:经济学家将各种商品和服务的价格合并为一个单一的价格水平.通货膨胀率只是价格水平的百分比变化。 然而,适用这一概念涉及一些实际困难。

p49.original: The Price of a Basket of Goods

p50.original: To calculate the price level, economists begin with the concept of a basket of goods and services, consisting of the different items individuals, businesses, or organizations typically buy. The next step is to look at how the prices of those items change over time. In thinking about how to combine individual prices into an overall price level, many people find that their first impulse is to calculate the average of the prices. Such a calculation, however, could easily be misleading because some products matter more than others.
p50.zh: 为了计算价格水平,经济学家首先提出一揽子商品和服务的概念,由个人、企业或组织通常购买的不同物品组成。下一步是研究这些物品的价格如何随时间而变化。 在思考如何将个别物价综合到整体物价水平时,许多人发现他们的第一个冲动是计算物价的平均值. 然而,这种计算容易引起误解,因为有些产品比其他产品更重要。

p51.original: Changes in the prices of goods for which people spend a larger share of their incomes will matter more than changes in the prices of goods for which people spend a smaller share of their incomes. For example, an increase of 10% in the rental rate on housing matters more to most people than whether the price of carrots rises by 10%. To construct an overall measure of the price level, economists compute a weighted average of the prices of the items in the basket, where the weights are based on the actual quantities of goods and services people buy. The following Work It Out feature walks you through the steps of calculating the annual rate of inflation based on a few products.
p51.zh: 人们花在收入中较大份额的商品价格的变动,将比人们花在收入中较少一部分的商品价格的变动更重要。 例如,住房租金增加10%对大多数人来说比胡萝卜价格是否上涨10%更重要。 为了构建价格水平的总体衡量标准,经济学家根据购买货物和服务的实际数量计算出篮子中物品价格的加权平均数。 以下的“工作”功能将您从几个产品中推导出, 来计算年通货膨胀率。

p123.original: To simplify the task of interpreting the price levels for more realistic and complex baskets of goods, economists typically report the price level in each period as an index number, rather than as the dollar amount for buying the basket of goods. Economists create price indices to calculate an overall average change in relative prices over time. To convert the money spent on the basket to an index number, economists arbitrarily choose one year to be the base year, or starting point from which we measure changes in prices. The base year, by definition, has an index number equal to 100. This sounds complicated, but it is really a simple math trick. In the example above, say that we choose time period 3  as the base year. Since the total amount of spending in that year is $107, we divide that amount by itself ($107) and multiply by 100. Again, this is because the index number in the base year always has to have a value of 100. Then, to figure out the values of the index number for the other years, we divide the dollar amounts for the other years by 1.07 as well. Note also that the dollar signs cancel out so that index numbers have no units.
p123.zh: 为了简化解释更现实和复杂的一揽子商品的价格水平的任务,经济学家通常将每个期间的价格水平作为一个指数编号,而不是作为购买一揽子商品的美元数额。经济学家创建价格指数,以计算长期相对价格的总体平均变化。 为了将花在篮子上的钱转换成一个指数,经济学家任意选择一年作为基年,或者从一个起点来衡量价格的变化. 按定义,基年的指数数等于100。 这听起来很复杂,但它确实是一个简单的数学伎俩。在上述例子中,说我们选择第3段作为基准年。 由于该年的总支出为107美元,我们自己将这一数额(107美元)除以100美元。这也是因为基年的指数总要达到100。 然后,为了计算其他年份的指数数字值,我们将其他年份的美元数额除以1.07。请注意,美元标志取消,使指数数字没有单位。

p147.original: If the inflation rate is the same whether it is based on dollar values or index numbers, then why bother with the index numbers? The advantage is that indexing allows easier eyeballing of the inflation numbers. If you glance at two index numbers like 107 and 110, you know automatically that the rate of inflation between the two years is about, but not quite exactly equal to, 3%. By contrast, imagine that we express the price levels in absolute dollars of a large basket of goods, so that when you looked at the data, the numbers were $19,493.62 and $20,040.17. Most people find it difficult to eyeball those kinds of numbers and say that it is a change of about 3%. However, the two numbers expressed in absolute dollars are exactly in the same proportion of 107 to 110 as the previous example. If you’re wondering why simple subtraction of the index numbers wouldn’t work, read the following Clear It Up feature.
p147.zh: 如果通货膨胀率是相同的,无论是基于美元价值还是指数数字,那么为什么还要费心去计算指数数字呢?其优点是指数化可以更容易地观察通货膨胀数字。 如果你看看107和110这样的两个指数, 你就会自动知道, 两年之间的通货膨胀率是大约,但并不完全等于3%。相比之下,想象一下,我们以一篮子大货品的绝对美元表示价格水平,这样,当你看数据时,数字是19 493.62美元和20 040.17美元。大多数人都觉得很难看清这些数字 并说这是大约3%的变化。 然而,以绝对美元表示的两个数字与前一个例子完全一样,在107比110的比例。 如果你想知道为什么简单的减除指数数字不会奏效,请读下“Clear It Up”的以下特征。

p148.original: Why do you not just subtract index numbers?
p148.zh: 你为什么不只是 减去指数数字?

p149.original: A word of warning: When a price index moves from, say, 107 to 110, the rate of inflation is not exactly 3%. Remember, the inflation rate is not derived by subtracting the index numbers, but rather through the percentage-change calculation. We calculate the precise inflation rate as the price index moves from 107 to 110 as 100 x (110 – 107) / 107 = 100 x 0.028 = 2.8%. When the base year is fairly close to 100, a quick subtraction is not a terrible shortcut to calculating the inflation rate—but when precision matters down to tenths of a percent, subtracting will not give the right answer.
p149.zh: 一个警告词:当一个价格指数从107到110, 通货膨胀率并不完全为3%。记住,通货膨胀率不是通过减去指数数字,而是通过百分比变化计算得出的。 随着价格指数从107升至110,我们计算出精确的通货膨胀率,为100x(110–107)/107=100x0.028=2.8%。 当基年相当接近100时,快速减法并不是计算通货膨胀率的可怕捷径 — — 但是当精确度降至十分之一时,减法不会给出正确的答案。

p150.original: Two final points about index numbers are worth remembering. First, index numbers have no dollar signs or other units attached to them. Although we can use index numbers to calculate a percentage inflation rate, the index numbers themselves do not have percentage signs. Index numbers just mirror the proportions that we find in other data. They transform the other data so that it is easier to work with the data.
p150.zh: 关于指数的最后两点值得记住。 首先,指数号没有美元标志或附着的其他单位. 虽然我们可以使用指数数字来计算一个百分率的通货膨胀率,但指数数字本身并没有百分率的标志.索引数字只是反映了我们在其他数据中找到的比例。 它们改变其他数据,以便更容易与数据合作。

p151.original: Second, the choice of a base year for the index number—that is, the year that is automatically set equal to 100—is arbitrary. We choose it as a starting point from which we can track changes in prices. In the official inflation statistics, it is common to use one base year for a few years, and then to update it, so that the base year of 100 is relatively close to the present. However, any base year that we choose for the index numbers will result in exactly the same inflation rate. To see this in the previous example, imagine that period 1 is the base year when total spending was $100, and we assign it an index number of 100. At a glance, you can see that the index numbers would now exactly match the dollar figures, and the inflation rate in the first period would be 6.5%.
p151.zh: 第二,为指数数字选择一个基年——即自动设定为100年——是任意的。 我们选择它作为一个起点,我们从这个起点上可以追踪价格的变化。 在官方的通货膨胀统计中,通常使用一个基年几年,然后更新,这样100的基年就比较接近现在. 然而,我们为指数数字选择的任何基年,将导致完全相同的通货膨胀率。 从前一个例子来看,想象1期是总开支为100美元的基年,我们给它分配了100个指数。 从一个角度看,你可以看到指数数字现在与美元数字完全吻合,第一个时期的通货膨胀率将是6.5%。

p152.original: Now that we see how indexes work to track inflation, the next module will show us how economists measure the cost of living.
p152.zh: 现在我们看到指数如何追踪通货膨胀, 下一个模块将告诉我们经济学家如何衡量生活成本。

p181.original: How to Measure Changes in the Cost of Living
p181.zh: 如何衡量生活费用的变化

p182.original: The most commonly cited measure of inflation in the United States is the Consumer Price Index (CPI). Government statisticians at the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics calculate the CPI based on the prices in a fixed basket of goods and services that represents the purchases of the average family of four. In recent years, the statisticians have paid considerable attention to a subtle problem: that the change in the total cost of buying a fixed basket of goods and services over time is conceptually not quite the same as the change in the cost of living, because the cost of living represents how much it costs for a person to feel that their consumption provides an equal level of satisfaction or utility.
p182.zh: 美国最常引用的通货膨胀衡量标准是消费价格指数(CPI). 美国的政府统计学家.劳动统计局根据代表平均四人家庭购买的固定一揽子商品和服务的价格计算消费物价指数。 近年来,统计人员相当关注一个微妙的问题:购买固定篮子商品和服务的总成本在概念上与生活成本的变化并不完全相同,因为生活成本代表着一个人觉得消费能提供同等程度的满足或效用需要付出多少代价.

p183.original: To understand the distinction, imagine that over the past 10 years, the cost of purchasing a fixed basket of goods increased by 25% and your salary also increased by 25%. Has your personal standard of living held constant? If you do not necessarily purchase an identical fixed basket of goods every year, then an inflation calculation based on the cost of a fixed basket of goods may be a misleading measure of how your cost of living has changed. Two problems arise here: substitution bias and quality/new goods bias.
p183.zh: 为了理解这种区别,想象一下,在过去10年里,购买固定篮子商品的成本增加了25%,而你的工资也增加了25%。 你的个人生活水平是否保持不变? 如果你不一定每年购买一个相同的固定篮子商品,那么根据固定篮子商品的成本计算通货膨胀,可能是对生活费用如何变化的误导性衡量. 这里出现了两个问题:替代偏差和质量/新商品偏差。

p184.original: When the price of a good rises, consumers tend to purchase less of it and to seek out substitutes instead. Conversely, as the price of a good falls, people will tend to purchase more of it. This pattern implies that goods with generally rising prices should tend over time to become less important in the overall basket of goods used to calculate inflation, while goods with falling prices should tend to become more important. Consider, as an example, a rise in the price of peaches by $100 per pound. If consumers were utterly inflexible in their demand for peaches, this would lead to a big rise in the price of food for consumers. Alternatively, imagine that people are utterly indifferent to whether they have peaches or other types of fruit. Now, if peach prices rise, people completely switch to other fruit choices and the average price of food does not change at all. A fixed and unchanging basket of goods assumes that consumers are locked into buying exactly the same goods, regardless of price changes—not a very likely assumption. Thus, substitution bias—the rise in the price of a fixed basket of goods over time—tends to overstate the rise in a consumer’s true cost of living, because it does not take into account that the person can substitute away from goods whose relative prices have risen.
p184.zh: 当商品价格上涨时,消费者往往购买较少商品,而是寻找替代品。 相反,随着好货的价格下跌,人们往往会购买更多的好货。 这种模式意味着价格普遍上涨的商品在计算通货膨胀的总的一揽子商品中应逐渐变得不那么重要,而价格下降的商品则应更加重要。以桃子每磅100美元的价格上涨为例. 如果消费者对桃子的需求完全不灵活,这将导致消费者食品价格的大幅上涨。 或者,想象一下,人们完全漠不关心自己是否拥有桃子或其他种类的水果. 现在,如果桃品价格上涨,人们完全转向其他水果选择,食物的平均价格根本不变.固定和不变的一揽子商品假设消费者被锁在购买完全相同的商品上,而不论价格变化如何,这并非一种极有可能的假设。 因此,替代偏差——固定篮子货物价格随时间推移而上涨——最终会过分夸大消费者真实生活成本的上涨,因为它没有考虑到个人可以替代相对价格上涨的商品。

p185.original: The other major problem in using a fixed basket of goods as the basis for calculating inflation is how to deal with the arrival of improved versions of older goods or altogether new goods. Consider the problem that arises if a cereal is improved by adding 12 essential vitamins and minerals—and also if a box of the cereal costs 5% more. It would clearly be misleading to count the entire resulting higher price as inflation, because the new price reflects a higher quality (or at least different) product. Ideally, one would like to know how much of the higher price is due to the quality change, and how much of it is just a higher price. The Bureau of Labor Statistics, which is responsible for computing the Consumer Price Index, must deal with these difficulties in adjusting for quality changes.
p185.zh: 使用固定篮子货物作为计算通货膨胀的基础的另一个主要问题是如何处理老旧货物或全新货物的改良版本的到来。考虑一下,如果通过增加12种基本维生素和矿物质来改善谷物,以及如果一盒谷物的价格增加5%,就会出现的问题。将由此带来的整个较高价格算作通货膨胀显然是误导性的,因为新价格反映了质量更高(或至少不同)的产品。理想的情况是,人们想知道,高价有多少是由于质量变化造成的,高价有多少只是较高的价格。负责计算消费物价指数的劳动统计局必须解决在调整质量变化方面的这些困难.

p186.original: Visit this website to view a list of Ford car prices between 1909 and 1927. Consider how these prices compare to today’s models. Is the product today of a different quality?

p187.original: We can think of a new product as an extreme improvement in quality—from something that did not exist to something that does. However, the basket of goods that was fixed in the past obviously does not include new goods created since then. The basket of goods and services in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) is revised and updated over time, and so new products are gradually included. However, the process takes some time. For example, room air conditioners were widely sold in the early 1950s, but were not introduced into the basket of goods behind the Consumer Price Index until 1964. The VCR and personal computer were available in the late 1970s and widely sold by the early 1980s, but did not enter the CPI basket of goods until 1987. By 1996, there were more than 40 million cellular phone subscribers in the United States—but cell phones were not yet part of the CPI basket of goods. The parade of inventions has continued, with the CPI inevitably lagging a few years behind.
p187.zh: 我们可以把新产品看作是质量的极端改善——从不存在的东西到确实存在的东西。 然而,过去固定的一揽子货物显然不包括此后创造的新货物。消费物价指数(CPI)中的商品与服务篮子随时间推移而修订和更新,因此逐渐纳入新产品. 然而,这一进程需要一些时间。 例如,房内空调在1950年代初期就被广泛出售,但直到1964年才被引入消费物价指数背后的篮子商品中.VCR和个人电脑在1970年代末期就已可使用,到1980年代初期已广泛销售,但直到1987年才进入CPI篮子商品. 到1996年,美国有超过4 000万移动电话用户,但移动电话尚未成为消费物价指数商品篮的一部分。发明的游行仍在继续,消费物价指数不可避免地落后了几年。

p188.original: The arrival of new goods creates problems with respect to the accuracy of measuring inflation. The reason people buy new goods, presumably, is that the new goods offer better value for money than existing goods. Thus, if the price index leaves out new goods, it overlooks one of the ways in which the cost of living is improving. In addition, the price of a new good is often higher when it is first introduced and then declines over time. If the new good is not included in the CPI for some years, until its price is already lower, the CPI may miss counting this price decline altogether. Taking these arguments together, the quality/new goods bias means that the rise in the price of a fixed basket of goods over time tends to overstate the rise in a consumer’s true cost of living, because it does not account for how improvements in the quality of existing goods or the invention of new goods improves the standard of living. The following Clear It Up feature is a must-read on how statisticians comprise and calculate the CPI.
p188.zh: 新商品的运抵给衡量通货膨胀的准确性造成了问题。 人们购买新商品的原因大概是,新商品比现有商品更能带来金钱价值。 因此,如果价格指数不列出新的商品,它忽视了生活费用正在提高的一种方式。 此外,新商品的价格在首次推出时往往更高,然后随时间推移而下降。 如果新商品在几年内没有被列入消费物价指数,直到其价格已经较低,消费物价指数可能完全没有计算这种价格下降。将这些论点综合起来,质量/新商品偏差意味着,固定篮子商品价格随时间推移而上涨,往往会过分夸大消费者真实生活成本的上涨,因为它没有考虑到现有商品质量的提高或新商品的发明如何提高生活水平。 以下的Clear It Up功能是统计师如何构成和计算消费物价指数的必读功能.

p189.original: How do U.S. government statisticians measure the Consumer Price Index?
p189.zh: 美国政府统计人员如何计量消费价格指数?.

p190.original: When the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) calculates the Consumer Price Index, the first task is to decide on a basket of goods that is representative of the purchases of the average household. We do this by using the Consumer Expenditure Survey, a national survey of about 7,000 households, which provides detailed information on spending habits. Statisticians divide consumer expenditures into eight major groups (seen below), which in turn they divide into more than 200 individual item categories. The BLS currently uses 1982–1984 as the base period.
p190.zh: 当美国.劳动统计局(BLS)计算消费物价指数,第一项任务是决定一个代表平均家庭购买的一揽子商品. 我们利用消费者支出调查来完成这项工作。 消费者支出调查是对大约7 000个家庭进行的全国调查,它提供了有关支出习惯的详细资料。统计人员将消费者支出分为八个主要类别(见下文),它们又分为200多个单独的项目类别。BLS目前使用1982–1984年作为基期.

p191.original: For each of the 200 individual expenditure items, the BLS chooses several hundred very specific examples of that item and looks at the prices of those examples. In figuring out the “breakfast cereal” item under the overall category of “foods and beverages,” the BLS picks several hundred examples of breakfast cereal. One example might be the price of a 24-oz. box of a particular brand of cereal sold at a particular store. The BLS statistically selects specific products and sizes and stores to reflect what people buy and where they shop. The basket of goods in the Consumer Price Index thus consists of about 80,000 products; that is, several hundred specific products in over 200 broad-item categories. Statisticians rotate about one-quarter of these 80,000 specific products of the sample each year, and replace them with a different set of products.
p191.zh: 对于200个个别支出项目,BLS选择了数百个非常具体的例子,并查看了这些例子的价格。 在“食品和饮料”这一总类别下,BLS在计算“早餐谷物”项目时,选取了几百个早餐谷物的例子。一个例子可能是某家商店销售的24美元谷类产品的价格。BLS在统计上选择了具体产品和大小以及商店,以反映人们购买什么和在哪里购物. 因此,消费物价指数中的一揽子商品包括大约80 000种产品,即200多个广泛项目类别的数百种具体产品。统计员每年轮换这8万个特定产品中的大约四分之一,用不同的产品组代替.

p192.original: The next step is to collect data on prices. Data collectors visit or call about 23,000 stores in 87 urban areas all over the United States every month to collect prices on these 80,000 specific products. The BLS also conducts a survey of 50,000 landlords or tenants to collect information about rents.
p192.zh: 下一步是收集有关价格的数据。数据收集员每月访问或拨打美国全国87个城市地区的约23000家商店,以收集这80,000种特定产品的价格.BLS还对5万房东或房客进行调查,以收集租金信息.

p193.original: Statisticians then calculate the Consumer Price Index by taking the 80,000 prices of individual products and combining them, using weights (see ) determined by the quantities of these products that people buy and allowing for factors like substitution between goods and quality improvements, into price indices for the 200 or so overall items. Then, the statisticians combine the price indices for the 200 items into an overall Consumer Price Index. According the Consumer Price Index website, there are eight categories that data collectors use:
p193.zh: 统计人员然后通过采用8万个单项产品的价格,将其合并计算消费物价指数,使用加权(见),根据人们购买的这些产品的数量确定,并允许替代商品和质量改进等因素,将这些价格指数纳入大约200个总项目的价格指数。 然后,统计人员将200个项目的价格指数合并为总体消费物价指数。 根据消费物价指数网站,数据收集者使用的有8个类别:

p194.original:
The Eight Major Categories in the Consumer Price Index
Food and beverages (breakfast cereal, milk, coffee, chicken, wine, full-service meals, and snacks)
Housing (renter’s cost of housing, homeowner’s cost of housing, fuel oil, bedroom furniture)
Apparel (men’s shirts and sweaters, women’s dresses, jewelry)
Transportation (new vehicles, airline fares, gasoline, motor vehicle insurance)
Medical care (prescription drugs and medical supplies, physicians’ services, eyeglasses and eye care, hospital services)
Recreation (televisions, cable television, pets and pet products, sports equipment, admissions)
Education and communication (college tuition, postage, telephone services, computer software and accessories)
Other goods and services (tobacco and smoking products, haircuts and other personal services, funeral expenses)
p194.zh: 消费物价指数中的八大类食品和饮料(早餐谷物、牛奶、咖啡、鸡、葡萄酒、全套餐饮和小吃) 住房(出租人住房费用、房主住房费用、燃料油、卧室家具) 服装(男衬衫和毛衣、女装、珠宝) 运输(新车、机票、汽油、机动车辆保险) 医疗(处方药和医疗用品、医生服务、眼镜和眼科护理、医院服务) 娱乐(电视、有线电视、宠物和宠物产品、体育设备、入院) 教育和通信(大学学费、邮资、电话服务、计算机软件和配件) 其他货物和服务(烟草和吸烟产品、理发和其他个人服务、丧葬费用)

p195.zh: 消费物价指数组成部分的加权

p196.original: The CPI and Core Inflation Index
p196.zh: 消费物价指数和核心通货膨胀指数

p197.original: Imagine if you were driving a company truck across the country- you probably would care about things like the prices of available roadside food and motel rooms as well as the truck’s operating condition.  However, the manager of the firm might have different priorities. He would care mostly about the truck’s on-time performance and much less so about the food you were eating and the places you were staying. In other words, the company manager would be paying attention to the firm's production, while ignoring transitory elements that impacted you, but did not affect the company’s bottom line.
p197.zh: 想象一下如果你开着一辆公司卡车横跨全国...你可能会关心诸如路边食品和汽车旅馆房间的价格以及卡车的运行状况。 但是,公司的经理可能有不同的优先次序。 他主要关心卡车的准时性能,换句话说,公司经理会注意公司的生产,而忽略影响你的过渡因素,但不影响公司的底线。

p198.original: In a sense, a similar situation occurs with regard to measures of inflation. As we’ve learned, CPI measures prices as they affect everyday household spending. Economists typically calculate a core inflation index by taking the CPI and excluding volatile economic variables. In this way, economists have a better sense of the underlying trends in prices that affect the cost of living.
p198.zh: 从某种意义上说,通货膨胀措施也出现了类似的情况。 我们了解到,消费物价指数衡量价格,因为价格影响日常家庭开支。经济学家通常通过采用消费物价指数和排除不稳定的经济变量来计算核心通货膨胀指数。 这样,经济学家对影响生活成本的价格的基本趋势有更好的认识.

p199.original: Examples of excluded variables include energy and food prices, which can jump around from month to month because of the weather. According to an article by Kent Bernhard, during Hurricane Katrina in 2005, a key supply point for the nation’s gasoline was nearly knocked out.  Gas prices quickly shot up across the nation, in some places by up to 40 cents a gallon in one day. This was not the cause of an economic policy but rather a short-lived event until the pumps were restored in the region. In this case, the CPI that month would register the change as a cost of living event to households, but the core inflation index would remain unchanged. As a result, the Federal Reserve’s decisions on interest rates would not be influenced.  Similarly, droughts can cause world-wide spikes in food prices that, if temporary, do not affect the nation’s economic capability.
p199.zh: 被排除在外的变量的例子包括能源和粮食价格,由于天气,能源和粮食价格可以逐月攀升。 根据肯特·伯恩哈德的文章,在2005年的飓风卡特里娜期间,该国汽油的关键供应点几乎被打晕。天然气价格迅速在全国上涨,在有些地方,一天内每加仑高达40美分. 这不是经济政策的原因,而是在该地区恢复水泵之前的短暂事件。 在这种情况下,当月的消费物价指数将这一变化登记为家庭的生活费用,但核心通货膨胀指数保持不变。 因此,美联储关于利率的决定不会受到影响。 同样,干旱也会导致全球粮食价格暴涨,如果是暂时的,不会影响国家的经济能力。

p200.original: As former Chairman of the Federal Reserve Ben Bernanke noted in 1999 about the core inflation index, “It provide(s) a better guide to monetary policy than the other indices, since it measures the more persistent underlying inflation rather than transitory influences on the price level.” Bernanke also noted that it helps communicate that the Federal Reserve does not need to respond to every inflationary shock since some price changes are transitory and not part of a structural change in the economy.
p200.zh: 正如前联邦储备局主席本·伯南克在1999年指出的,“它比其他指数更能指导货币政策,因为它衡量的是更持久的基本通货膨胀,而不是价格水平的暂时性影响。” 伯南克还指出,它有助于宣传,由于一些价格变化是暂时性的,而不是经济结构变化的一部分,所以联邦储备局不需要对每一次通货膨胀冲击作出反应。

p201.original: In sum, both the CPI and the core inflation index are important, but serve different audiences. The CPI helps households understand their overall cost of living from month to month, while the core inflation index is a preferred gauge from which to make important government policy changes.
p201.zh: 总之,消费物价指数和核心通胀指数都很重要,但服务于不同的受众.消费物价指数帮助家庭了解他们每月的总体生活成本,而核心通货膨胀指数则是政府政策作出重要改变的首选衡量标准。

p202.original: Practical Solutions for the Substitution and the Quality/New Goods Biases
p202.zh: 替代和质量/新货物比喻的实际解决办法

p203.original: By the early 2000s, the Bureau of Labor Statistics was using alternative mathematical methods for calculating the Consumer Price Index, more complicated than just adding up the cost of a fixed basket of goods, to allow for some substitution between goods. It was also updating the basket of goods behind the CPI more frequently, so that it could include new and improved goods more rapidly. For certain products, the BLS was carrying out studies to try to measure the quality improvement. For example, with computers, an economic study can try to adjust for changes in speed, memory, screen size, and other product characteristics, and then calculate the change in price after accounting for these product changes. However, these adjustments are inevitably imperfect, and exactly how to make these adjustments is often a source of controversy among professional economists.
p203.zh: 到2000年代初,劳工统计局正在使用替代的数学方法计算消费物价指数,比仅仅将固定篮子商品的成本相加更为复杂,以便在商品之间进行某种替代. 它还更经常地更新消费物价指数背后的一揽子商品,以便它能够更快地包括新的和改良的商品。 对于某些产品,BLS正在进行研究,试图衡量质量的提高。 例如,用计算机,经济研究可以尝试调整速度,内存,屏幕大小等产品特性的变化,然后在计算这些产品变化后计算价格变化. 然而,这些调整不可避免地是不完善的,准确的如何做出这些调整往往引起专业经济学家的争议.

p204.original: By the early 2000s, the substitution bias and quality/new goods bias had been somewhat reduced, so that since then the rise in the CPI probably overstates the true rise in inflation by only about 0.5% per year. Over one or a few years, this is not much. Over a period of a decade or two, even half of a percent per year compounds to a more significant amount. In addition, the CPI tracks prices from physical locations, and not at online sites like Amazon, where prices can be lower.
p204.zh: 到2000年代初期,替代偏差和质量/新商品偏差有所降低,因此自此以后,消费物价指数的上升可能夸大了通货膨胀的实际上升,每年只增加约0.5%。一年或几年时间里,情况并不严重。 在一二十年的时间里,甚至每年有一半的金额会增加很多。 此外,消费物价指数还从实际地点追踪价格,而不是在亚马逊等在线网站追踪价格,因为那里的物价可以降低.

p205.original: When measuring inflation (and other economic statistics, too), a tradeoff arises between simplicity and interpretation. If we calculate the inflation rate with a basket of goods that is fixed and unchanging, then the calculation of an inflation rate is straightforward, but the problems of substitution bias and quality/new goods bias will arise. However, when the basket of goods is allowed to shift and evolve to reflect substitution toward lower relative prices, quality improvements, and new goods, the technical details of calculating the inflation rate grow more complex.
p205.zh: 在衡量通货膨胀(以及其他经济统计)时,在简洁和解释之间产生权衡。 如果我们用一篮固定不变的商品计算通货膨胀率,那么计算通货膨胀率就简单明了了,但替代偏差和质量/新商品偏差的问题将出现。 然而,当允许一篮子商品转移和演变,以反映替代物向相对价格较低、质量提高和新商品发展时,计算通货膨胀率的技术细节就变得更加复杂。

p206.original: Additional Price Indices: PPI, GDP Deflator, and More
p206.zh: 附加价格指数:PPI、GDP减缩指数和更多

p207.original: The basket of goods behind the Consumer Price Index represents an average hypothetical U.S. household's consumption, which is to say that it does not exactly capture anyone’s personal experience. When the task is to calculate an average level of inflation, this approach works fine. What if, however, you are concerned about inflation experienced by a certain group, like the elderly, or the poor, or single-parent families with children, or Hispanic-Americans? In specific situations, a price index based on the buying power of the average consumer may not feel quite right.
p207.zh: 消费物价指数背后的篮子商品代表了美国家庭的平均消费假设,也就是说它并不完全能捕捉到任何人的个人经历. 当任务是计算平均通货膨胀水平时,这一办法效果良好。 但是,如果你担心某个群体的通货膨胀, 比如老人,穷人,或者有孩子的单亲家庭,或者西班牙裔美国人?在特定情况下,基于一般消费者购买力的价格指数可能不觉得相当正确。

p208.original: This problem has a straightforward solution. If the Consumer Price Index does not serve the desired purpose, then invent another index, based on a basket of goods appropriate for the group of interest. The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes a number of experimental price indices: some for particular groups like the elderly or the poor, some for different geographic areas, and some for certain broad categories of goods like food or housing.
p208.zh: 这个问题有一个直截了当的解决办法。 如果消费物价指数不能达到预期目的,则根据适合利益集团的一揽子商品,制定另一个指数。劳工统计局公布一些试验性价格指数:一些是针对老年人或穷人等特定群体的,有些是针对不同地理区域的,有些是针对食品或住房等某些大类商品的。

p209.original: The BLS also calculates several price indices that are not based on baskets of consumer goods. For example, the Producer Price Index (PPI) is based on prices paid for supplies and inputs by producers of goods and services. We can break it down into price indices for different industries, commodities, and stages of processing (like finished goods, intermediate goods, or crude materials for further processing). There is an International Price Index based on the prices of merchandise that is exported or imported. An Employment Cost Index measures wage inflation in the labor market. The GDP deflator, which the Bureau of Economic Analysis measures, is a price index that includes all the GDP components (that is, consumption plus investment plus government plus exports minus imports). Unlike the CPI, its baskets are not fixed but re-calculate what that year’s GDP would have been worth using the base-year’s prices. MIT's Billion Prices Project is a more recent alternative attempt to measure prices: economists collect data online from retailers and then put them into an index that they compare to the CPI (Source: http://bpp.mit.edu/usa/).
p209.zh: BLS还计算了几种不以篮子消费品为基础的价格指数. 例如,生产者价格指数是根据货物和服务生产者为供应品和投入支付的价格编制的。 我们可以将其细分为不同行业、商品和加工阶段的价格指数(如制成品、中间货物或供进一步加工的原油)。有一项基于进出口商品价格的国际价格指数。就业成本指数衡量劳动力市场的工资通货膨胀。经济分析局衡量的国内总产值减缩指数是包含所有国内总产值组成部分(即消费加投资加政府出口减进口)的价格指数。与消费物价指数不同的是,其篮子不是固定的,而是重新计算该年的国内生产总值用基年价格计算的价值。麻省理工学院的"十亿价格项目"是比较近期的衡量价格的另类尝试:经济学家通过在线从零售商那里收集数据,然后将其放入一个指数,与CPI进行比较(资料来源:http://bpp.mit.edu/usa/).

p210.original: What’s the best measure of inflation? If one is concerned with the most accurate measure of inflation, one should use the GDP deflator as it picks up the prices of goods and services produced. However, it is not a good measure of the cost of living as it includes prices of many products not purchased by households (for example, aircraft, fire engines, factory buildings, office complexes, and bulldozers). If one wants the most accurate measure of inflation as it impacts households, one should use the CPI, as it only picks up prices of products purchased by households. That is why economists sometimes refer to the CPI as the cost-of-living index. As the Bureau of Labor Statistics states on its website: “The ‘best’ measure of inflation for a given application depends on the intended use of the data.”
p210.zh: 通货膨胀的最佳衡量标准是什么? 如果人们关心最准确的通货膨胀衡量标准,就应该使用国内生产总值的减缩指数,因为这一指数可以提高所生产的货物和服务的价格。 然而,它并不是衡量生活成本的好办法,因为它包括许多家庭没有购买的产品的价格(例如飞机、消防机、工厂建筑、办公楼和推土机)。 如果人们想要对影响家庭的通货膨胀进行最准确的衡量,就应该使用消费物价指数,因为消费物价指数只是提高家庭购买的产品的价格。 因此,经济学家有时将消费物价指数称为生活费指数。 正如劳工统计局在其网站上指出的,“特定应用的通货膨胀`最佳 ' 衡量标准取决于数据的预期用途。”

p212.original: Measuring price levels with a fixed basket of goods will always have two problems: the substitution bias, by which a fixed basket of goods does not allow for buying more of what becomes relatively less expensive and less of what becomes relatively more expensive; and the quality/new goods bias, by which a fixed basket cannot account for improvements in quality and the advent of new goods. These problems can be reduced in degree—for example, by allowing the basket of goods to evolve over time—but we cannot totally eliminate them. The most commonly cited measure of inflation is the Consumer Price Index (CPI), which is based on a basket of goods representing what the typical consumer buys. The Core Inflation Index further breaks down the CPI by excluding volatile economic commodities. Several price indices are not based on baskets of consumer goods. The GDP deflator is based on all GDP components. The Producer Price Index is based on prices of supplies and inputs bought by producers of goods and services. An Employment Cost Index measures wage inflation in the labor market. An International Price Index is based on the prices of merchandise that is exported or imported.
p212.zh: 用固定篮子衡量价格水平总是有两个问题:替代偏差,即固定篮子不允许购买更多相对便宜的货物,而较少购买更多相对昂贵的货物;质量/新商品偏差,即固定篮子无法说明质量的提高和新商品的出现。这些问题可以减少程度,例如,通过让一篮子货物随时间演变,但我们不能完全消除它们。 最常提到的通货膨胀衡量标准是消费价格指数(CPI),该指数基于代表典型消费购买的一篮子商品.核心通货膨胀指数将不稳定的经济商品排除在外,从而进一步打破消费物价指数。 若干价格指数不是以消费品篮子为基础的。GDP减缩指数基于所有GDP部分.生产者价格指数是根据货物和服务生产者购买的供应品和投入的价格编制的。就业成本指数衡量劳动力市场的工资通货膨胀。 国际价格指数以进出口商品的价格为基础。

p214.original: How to Measure Changes in the Cost of Living introduced a number of different price indices. Which price index would be best to use to adjust your paycheck for inflation?
p214.zh: 如何衡量生活费用的变化,引入了一些不同的价格指数。哪个价格指数最适合用来调整通货膨胀的薪资?

p215.original: Since the CPI measures the prices of the goods and services purchased by the typical urban consumer, it measures the prices of things that people buy with their paycheck. For that reason, the CPI would be the best price index to use for this purpose.
p215.zh: 由于消费物价指数衡量的是典型的城市消费者购买的商品和服务的价格,因此它衡量的是人们用工资购买的东西的价格. 因此,消费物价指数将是用于这一目的的最佳价格指数。

p216.original: The Consumer Price Index is subject to the substitution bias and the quality/new goods bias. Are the Producer Price Index and the GDP Deflator also subject to these biases? Why or why not?
p216.zh: 消费者价格指数受制于替代偏差和质量/新商品偏差。生产者价格指数和国内生产总值减缩指数是否也受到这些偏见的影响? 为什么或为什么不呢?

p217.original: The PPI is subject to those biases for essentially the same reasons as the CPI is. The GDP deflator picks up prices of what is actually purchased that year, so there are no biases. That is the advantage of using the GDP deflator over the CPI.
p217.zh: 私人消费物价指数受到这些偏见的影响,其原因与消费物价指数基本相同。国内生产总值的减缩指数提高了当年实际购买物的价格,因此没有偏见。 这就是使用国内生产总值减缩指数而不是消费物价指数的优势。

p219.original: Why does “substitution bias” arise if we calculate the inflation rate based on a fixed basket of goods?
p219.zh: 如果我们根据一篮固定货物计算通货膨胀率,为什么会出现“替代偏差”?

p220.original: Why does the “quality/new goods bias” arise if we calculate the inflation rate based on a fixed basket of goods?
p220.zh: 如果我们根据一篮固定货物计算通货膨胀率,为什么会出现“质量/新货物偏差”?

p222.original: Given the federal budget deficit in recent years, some economists have argued that by adjusting Social Security payments for inflation using the CPI, Social Security is overpaying recipients. What is their argument, and do you agree or disagree with it?
p222.zh: 鉴于近年来的联邦预算赤字,一些经济学家认为,通过使用消费物价指数调整社会保障支付通货膨胀,社会保障是多付的受保人. 他们的论点是什么,你同意还是不同意?

p223.original: Why is the GDP deflator not an accurate measure of inflation as it impacts a household?
p223.zh: 为什么国内生产总值的减缩指数不是影响家庭的通货膨胀的准确衡量标准?

p224.original: Imagine that the government statisticians who calculate the inflation rate have been updating the basic basket of goods once every 10 years, but now they decide to update it every five years. How will this change affect the amount of substitution bias and quality/new goods bias?
p224.zh: 想象一下计算通货膨胀率的政府统计人员每十年更新一次基本商品篮子,但现在他们决定每五年更新一次. 这一变化将如何影响替代偏差和质量/新商品偏差的程度?

p225.original: Describe a situation, either a government policy situation, an economic problem, or a private sector situation, where using the CPI to convert from nominal to real would be more appropriate than using the GDP deflator.
p225.zh: 描述一种情况,即政府的政策情况、经济问题或私营部门的情况,利用消费物价指数从名义上转变为实际,比使用国内生产总值减缩指数更为恰当。

p226.original: Describe a situation, either a government policy situation, an economic problem, or a private sector situation, where using the GDP deflator to convert from nominal to real would be more appropriate than using the CPI.
p226.zh: 描述一种情况,即政府的政策情况、经济问题或私营部门的情况,利用国内生产总值减缩指数从名义上转化为实际,比使用消费物价指数更合适。

p230.original: How the U.S. and Other Countries Experience Inflation
p230.zh: 美国和其他国家是如何经历通货膨胀的

p231.original: In the last three decades, inflation has been relatively low in the U.S. economy, with the Consumer Price Index typically rising 2% to 4% per year. Looking back over the twentieth century, there have been several periods where inflation caused the price level to rise at double-digit rates, but nothing has come close to hyperinflation.
p231.zh: 在过去的三十年里,美国经济的通货膨胀一直相对较低,消费物价指数通常每年上升2%至4%. 回顾20世纪,曾有数个时期通货膨胀导致物价水平以两位数的速率上升,但没有什么事情接近恶性通货膨胀。

p232.original: Historical Inflation in the U.S. Economy
p232.zh: 美国历史通货膨胀.经济

p233.original: (a) shows the level of prices in the Consumer Price Index stretching back to 1913. In this case, the base years (when the CPI is defined as 100) are set for the average level of prices that existed from 1982 to 1984.  (b) shows the annual percentage changes in the CPI over time, which is the inflation rate.
p233.zh: (a) 显示可追溯到1913年的消费物价指数的价格水平。 在这种情况下,基准年(消费物价指数定义为100年时)是确定1982年至1984年的平均价格水平的。(b) 显示消费物价指数随时间推移的年度百分比变化,即通货膨胀率。

p234.original: U.S. Price Level and Inflation Rates since 1947
p234.zh: 美国.1947年以来的价格水平和通货膨胀率

p235.original: Inflation as measured by the consumer price index reflects the annual percentage change in the cost to the average consumer of acquiring a basket of goods and services that may be fixed or changed at specified intervals, such as yearly.
p235.zh: 按消费物价指数衡量的通货膨胀反映了购买一揽子货物和服务的费用每年对一般消费者的百分比变化,这些货物和服务可以按规定的时间间隔固定或改变,例如每年一次。

p236.original: The first two waves of inflation are easy to characterize in historical terms: they are right after World War I and World War II. However, there are also two periods of severe negative inflation—called deflation—in the early decades of the twentieth century: one following the deep 1920-21 recession and the other during the Great Depression of the 1930s. (Since inflation is a time when the buying power of money in terms of goods and services is reduced, deflation will be a time when the buying power of money in terms of goods and services increases.) For the period from 1900 to about 1960, the major inflations and deflations nearly balanced each other out, so the average annual rate of inflation over these years was only about 1% per year. A third wave of more severe inflation arrived in the 1970s and departed in the early 1980s.
p236.zh: 最初的两波通货膨胀从历史角度来说很容易被定性:它们正好在第一次世界大战和二战之后. 然而,在20世纪早期的几十年中,还有两个时期出现严重的负通货膨胀,即所谓的通货紧缩:一个时期是在1920-21年深陷衰退之后,另一个时期是在1930年代的大萧条期间。(由于通货膨胀是货币在商品和服务方面的购买力下降的时期,通货紧缩将是货币在商品和服务方面的购买力增加的时期. )从1900年到大约1960年,主要通货膨胀和通货紧缩几乎相互平衡,所以这些年的平均年通货膨胀率每年只有1%左右.1970年代第三波更严重的通货膨胀到达,1980年代初离开.

p237.original: Visit this website to use an inflation calculator and discover how prices have changed in the last 100 years.
p237.zh: 访问这个网站,使用通货膨胀计算器,并发现价格在过去100年里是如何变化的.

p238.original: Times of recession or depression often seem to be times when the inflation rate is lower, as in the recession of 1920–1921, the Great Depression, the recession of 1980–1982, and the Great Recession in 2008–2009. There were a few months in 2009 that were deflationary, but not at an annual rate. High levels of unemployment typically accompany recessions, and the total demand for goods falls, pulling the price level down. Conversely, the rate of inflation often, but not always, seems to start moving up when the economy is growing very strongly, like right after wartime or during the 1960s. The frameworks for macroeconomic analysis, that we developed in other chapters, will explain why recession often accompanies higher unemployment and lower inflation, while rapid economic growth often brings lower unemployment but higher inflation.
p238.zh: 衰退或萧条的时代往往似乎是通货膨胀率较低的时候,例如1920-1921年的衰退、大萧条、1980-1982年的衰退和2008-2009年的大衰退。2009年有几个月出现通货紧缩,但没有达到每年的通货紧缩率。失业率高通常伴随着经济衰退,对商品的总需求下降,使价格水平下降。反之,当经济非常强劲增长时,通货膨胀率往往但并不总是开始上升,比如战后或1960年代。 我们在其他章节中制定的宏观经济分析框架将解释为什么衰退往往伴随着失业率上升和通货膨胀率降低,而快速的经济增长往往带来失业率降低,但通货膨胀率上升。

p240.original: Around the rest of the world, the pattern of inflation has been very mixed;  shows inflation rates over the last several decades. Many industrialized countries, not just the United States, had relatively high inflation rates in the 1970s. For example, in 1975, Japan’s inflation rate was over 8% and the inflation rate for the United Kingdom was almost 25%. In the 1980s, inflation rates came down in the United States and in Europe and have largely stayed down.
p240.zh: 在世界其他地方,通货膨胀模式参差不齐;显示过去几十年的通货膨胀率。 许多工业化国家,不仅仅是美国,在1970年代通货膨胀率相对较高。 例如,在1975年,日本的通货膨胀率超过8%,联合王国的通货膨胀率接近25%。20世纪80年代,美国和欧洲的通货膨胀率下降,并基本保持低水平.

p241.original: Countries with Relatively Low Inflation Rates, 1961–2020
p241.zh: 1961-2020年通货膨胀率相对较低的国家

p242.original: Countries with controlled economies in the 1970s, like the Soviet Union and China, historically had very low rates of measured inflation—because prices were forbidden to rise by law, except for the cases where the government deemed a price increase to be due to quality improvements. However, these countries also had perpetual shortages of goods, since forbidding prices to rise acts like a price ceiling and creates a situation where quantity demanded often exceeds quantity supplied. As Russia and China made a transition toward more market-oriented economies, they also experienced outbursts of inflation, although we should regard the statistics for these economies as somewhat shakier. Inflation in China averaged about 10% per year for much of the 1980s and early 1990s, although it has dropped off since then. Russia experienced hyperinflation—an outburst of high inflation—of 2,500% per year in the early 1990s, although by 2006 Russia’s consumer price inflation had dipped below 10% per year, as  shows. The closest the United States has ever reached hyperinflation was during the 1860–1865 Civil War, in the Confederate states.
p242.zh: 1970年代经济受到控制的国家,如苏联和中国,历史上测量的通货膨胀率非常低——因为法律禁止价格上涨,但政府认为价格上涨是由于质量改善所致的情况除外。 然而,这些国家也长期缺乏货物,因为禁止价格上涨的行为类似于最高物价,造成需求量往往超过供应量的情况。 随着俄罗斯和中国向更面向市场的经济体过渡,它们也经历了通货膨胀暴涨,尽管我们应当认为这些经济体的统计数据比较不稳定。1980年代和1990年代初,中国的年平均通货膨胀率大约为10%,尽管此后有所下降。 俄罗斯在20世纪90年代早期曾经历了每年2500 %的恶性通货膨胀 — — 高通胀的暴发,不过,如上表所示,到2006年,俄罗斯的消费物价通胀已经下降到每年10 %以下。 美国最接近的恶性通货膨胀是在1860-1865年内战期间,在邦联各州。

p243.original: Countries with Relatively High Inflation Rates, 1981–2020
p243.zh: 1981-2020年通货膨胀率相对较高的国家

p244.original: Many countries in Latin America experienced raging inflation during the 1980s and early 1990s, with inflation rates often well above 100% per year. In 1990, for example, both Brazil and Argentina saw inflation climb above 2000%. Certain countries in Africa experienced extremely high rates of inflation, sometimes bordering on hyperinflation, in the 1990s. Nigeria, the most populous country in Africa, had an inflation rate of 75% in 1995.
p244.zh: 拉丁美洲许多国家在1980年代和1990年代初经历了剧烈的通货膨胀,每年的通货膨胀率往往大大高于100%。 例如,1990年,巴西和阿根廷的通货膨胀率都超过了2000 %。1990年代,非洲一些国家的通货膨胀率极高,有时接近恶性通货膨胀。 尼日利亚是非洲人口最多的国家,1995年的通货膨胀率为75%。

p245.original: In the early 2000s, the problem of inflation appears to have diminished for most countries, at least in comparison to the worst times of recent decades. As we noted in this earlier Bring it Home feature, in recent years, the world’s worst example of hyperinflation was in Zimbabwe, where at one point the government was issuing bills with a face value of $100 trillion (in Zimbabwean dollars)—that is, the bills had $100,000,000,000,000 written on the front, but were almost worthless. In many countries, the memory of double-digit, triple-digit, and even quadruple-digit inflation is not very far in the past.
p245.zh: 在2000年代初期,大多数国家的通货膨胀问题似乎已经减少,至少与最近几十年最糟糕的时期相比是如此。 正如我们早些时候在“带回家”中指出的那样, 近年来, 世界上恶性通货膨胀最糟糕的例子是津巴布韦, 津巴布韦政府一度发行面值为100万亿美元的法案,在许多国家,过去对两位数,三位数,甚至四位数通货膨胀的记忆并不很长.

p247.original: In the U.S. economy, the annual inflation rate in the last two decades has typically been around 2% to 4%. The periods of highest inflation in the United States in the twentieth century occurred during the years after World Wars I and II, and in the 1970s. The period of lowest inflation—actually, with deflation—was the 1930s Great Depression.
p247.zh: 在美国经济中,过去20年的年通货膨胀率一般在2%到4%左右.20世纪美国通货膨胀最高的时期发生在第一次和第二次世界大战之后的几年中,以及1970年代.通货膨胀最低的时期——事实上,通货紧缩——是1930年代的大萧条。

p249.zh: 腾讯这个网站的购买力计算器 at measingWorth.com. 今天要花多少钱才能买到 你出生的那年买的一块钱?

p252.zh: 以购买力来说,你想要转换的金额

p253.zh: 最后一年——现在或最近一年,计算器将接受
