p256.original: What has been a typical range of inflation in the U.S. economy in the last decade or so?
p256.zh: 过去十年左右,美国经济中典型的通货膨胀范围是什么?

p257.original: Over the last century, during what periods was the U.S. inflation rate highest and lowest?
p257.zh: 在过去一个世纪中,美国通货膨胀率在什么时期是最高和最低的?

p260.original: Why do you think the U.S. experience with inflation over the last 50 years has been so much milder than in many other countries?
p260.zh: 为什么美国过去50年的通货膨胀经验比其他许多国家要温和得多?

p262.original: Within 1 or 2 percentage points, what has the U.S. inflation rate been during the last 20 years? Draw a graph to show the data.
p262.zh: 在1或2个百分点之内,美国在过去20年的通货膨胀率是多少?绘制图表以显示数据。

p264.original: Economists usually oppose high inflation, but they oppose it in a milder way than many non-economists. Robert Shiller, one of 2013’s Nobel Prize winners in economics, carried out several surveys during the 1990s about attitudes toward inflation. One of his questions asked, “Do you agree that preventing high inflation is an important national priority, as important as preventing drug use or preventing deterioration in the quality of our schools?” Answers were on a scale of 1–5, where 1 meant “Fully agree” and 5 meant “Completely disagree.” For the U.S. population as a whole, 52% answered “Fully agree” that preventing high inflation was a highly important national priority and just 4% said “Completely disagree.” However, among professional economists, only 18% answered “Fully agree,” while the same percentage of 18% answered “Completely disagree.”
p264.zh: 经济学家通常反对高通胀,但他们反对的方式比许多非经济学家要温和.2013年诺贝尔经济学奖得主之一罗伯特·希勒(Robert Shiller)在20世纪90年代对通货膨胀的态度进行了几次调查。 他问到的一个问题是,“你是否同意防止高通胀是国家的重要优先事项,与防止吸毒或防止我们学校质量恶化同样重要? ”答案是1-5的尺度,其中1个意思是“完全同意 ” , 5个意思是“完全不同意 ” 。 对于美国全体人民来说,52%的人回答“完全同意 ” , “ 完全同意 ” , 而只有4%的人回答“完全不同意 ” 。 然而,在专业经济学家中,只有18%的人回答“完全同意 ” , 而18%的人回答“完全不同意 ” 。

p266.original: What are the economic problems caused by inflation, and why do economists often regard them with less concern than the general public? Consider a very short story: “The Land of Funny Money.”
p266.zh: 通货膨胀造成的经济问题是什么,为什么经济学家往往比普通大众更关心这些问题?想想一个很短的故事:“有趣的钱之地”。

p267.original: One morning, everyone in the Land of Funny Money awakened to find that everything denominated in money had increased by 20%. The change was completely unexpected. Every price in every store was 20% higher. Paychecks were 20% higher. Interest rates were 20 % higher. The amount of money, everywhere from wallets to savings accounts, was 20% larger. This overnight inflation of prices made newspaper headlines everywhere in the Land of Funny Money. However, the headlines quickly disappeared, as people realized that in terms of what they could actually buy with their incomes, this inflation had no economic impact. Everyone’s pay could still buy exactly the same set of goods as it did before. Everyone’s savings were still sufficient to buy exactly the same car, vacation, or retirement that they could have bought before. Equal levels of inflation in all wages and prices ended up not mattering much at all.
p267.zh: 一天早上,有趣的钱庄的每个人醒来发现,所有以钱计价的东西都增加了20%.变化是完全出乎意料的。 每家店的每个价格都高了20%.薪资提高20%。利率提高了20%。 从钱包到储蓄账户, 钱的金额都大了20%。一夜之间价格的暴涨 成为了报纸的头条新闻 在有趣的钱之地。 然而,头条新闻很快就消失了,因为人们意识到,从他们用收入实际能够买到的东西来看,这种通货膨胀并没有产生任何经济影响.每个人的薪水仍然可以买到和以前完全一样的一套商品。每个人的储蓄仍然足以购买他们以前可以购买的完全相同的汽车、假期或退休。在所有工资和价格方面,通货膨胀水平相同,但最终完全无关紧要。

p268.original: When the people in Robert Shiller’s surveys explained their concern about inflation, one typical reason was that they feared that as prices rose, they would not be able to afford to buy as much. In other words, people were worried because they did not live in a place like the Land of Funny Money, where all prices and wages rose simultaneously. Instead, people live here on Planet Earth, where prices might rise while wages do not rise at all, or where wages rise more slowly than prices.
p268.zh: 当罗伯特·希勒调查中的人解释他们对通货膨胀的担忧时,一个典型的原因是他们担心随着物价上涨,他们买不起那么多钱.换句话说,人们之所以担心,是因为他们没有生活在一个像"有趣的钱之地"这样的地方,那里所有的物价和工资都同时上涨. 相反,人们生活在地球星球上,那里的物价可能会上涨,而工资却根本不上涨,或者工资的上涨比物价慢。

p269.original: Economists note that over most periods, the inflation level in prices is roughly similar to the inflation level in wages, and so they reason that, on average, over time, people’s economic status is not greatly changed by inflation. If all prices, wages, and interest rates adjusted automatically and immediately with inflation, as in the Land of Funny Money, then no one’s purchasing power, profits, or real loan payments would change. However, if other economic variables do not move exactly in sync with inflation, or if they adjust for inflation only after a time lag, then inflation can cause three types of problems: unintended redistributions of purchasing power, blurred price signals, and difficulties in long-term planning.
p269.zh: 经济学家指出,在大多数时期,物价的通胀水平与工资的通胀水平大致相似,因此他们认为,随着时间的推移,人们的经济地位并没有因通货膨胀而发生很大变化。 如果所有的价格、工资和利率都随通货膨胀而自动和立即调整,如在有趣的钱庄,那么,没有人会改变购买力、利润或实际贷款支付。 然而,如果其他经济变量没有与通货膨胀完全同步移动,或者只有在一段时间后才根据通货膨胀进行调整,那么通货膨胀就可能造成三类问题:购买力的意外再分配,价格信号模糊,以及长期规划方面的困难.

p271.original: Inflation can cause redistributions of purchasing power that hurt some and help others. People who are hurt by inflation include those who are holding considerable cash, whether it is in a safe deposit box or in a cardboard box under the bed. When inflation happens, the buying power of cash diminishes. However, cash is only an example of a more general problem: anyone who has financial assets invested in a way that the nominal return does not keep up with inflation will tend to be affected by inflation. For example, if a person has money in a bank account that pays 4% interest, but inflation rises to 5%, then the real rate of return for the money invested in that bank account is negative 1%.
p271.zh: 通货膨胀可能导致购买力的再分配,从而伤害到一些人,帮助其他人。受通货膨胀伤害的人包括那些持有大量现金的人,无论是在保险箱里还是在床底下的纸箱里. 当通货膨胀发生时,现金的购买力就会减弱. 然而,现金只是一个更普遍问题的例子:任何金融资产投资方式使名义收益无法跟上通货膨胀的人,都会受到通货膨胀的影响。 例如,如果一个人在支付4%利息的银行账户中拥有资金,但通货膨胀上升至5%,那么该银行账户中投资的资金的实际回报率为负1%。

p272.original: The problem of a good-looking nominal interest rate transforming into an ugly-looking real interest rate can be worsened by taxes. The U.S. income tax is charged on the nominal interest received in dollar terms, without an adjustment for inflation. Thus, the government taxes a person who invests $10,000 and receives a 5% nominal rate of interest on the $500 received—no matter whether the inflation rate is 0%, 5%, or 10%. If inflation is 0%, then the real interest rate is 5% and all $500 is a gain in buying power. However, if inflation is 5%, then the real interest rate is zero and the person had no real gain—but owes income tax on the nominal gain anyway. If inflation is 10%, then the real interest rate is negative 5% and the person is actually falling behind in buying power, but would still owe taxes on the $500 in nominal gains.
p272.zh: 名义利率看起来不错,而实际利率看起来丑陋,而税收则可能使这一问题恶化。 美国所得税按收到的名义利息以美元计征,不因通货膨胀进行调整. 因此,政府向投资1万美元的人征税,对收到的500美元收取5%的名义利率——无论通货膨胀率是0%、5%还是10%。 如果通货膨胀为0%,那么实际利率为5%,所有500美元都是购买力的增益. 然而,如果通货膨胀为5%,那么实际利率为零,而且此人没有实际收益——但无论如何,他必须缴纳名义收益的所得税。 如果通货膨胀为10%,那么实际利率为负5%,而且此人实际上在购买权方面落在后面,但仍会欠500美元名义收益的税。

p273.original: Inflation can cause unintended redistributions for wage earners, too. Wages do typically creep up with inflation over time, eventually. The last row of  at the start of this chapter showed that the average hourly wage in manufacturing in the U.S. economy increased from $3.23 in 1970 to $30.11 in 2021, which is an increase by a factor of close to ten. Over that time period, the Consumer Price Index increased by about a factor of eight. However, increases in wages may lag behind inflation for a year or two, since wage adjustments are often somewhat sticky and occur only once or twice a year. Moreover, the extent to which wages keep up with inflation creates insecurity for workers and may involve painful, prolonged conflicts between employers and employees. If the government adjusts minimum wage for inflation only infrequently, minimum wage workers are losing purchasing power from their nominal wages, as  shows.
p273.zh: 通货膨胀也会导致工资劳动者意外地再分配。工资往往随时间推移而上升。本章开头的最后一行显示,美国经济制造业的平均小时工资从1970年的3.23美元增加到2021年的30.11美元,增加了近10倍.在此期间,消费物价指数上升了大约八倍。 然而,工资增长可能落后于一年或两年的通货膨胀,因为工资调整往往有些粘滞,一年只发生一两次. 此外,工资与通货膨胀保持同步的程度给工人带来不安全,并可能涉及雇主和雇员之间痛苦和长期的冲突。 如果政府只是偶尔对最低工资进行调整,最低工资工人就会失去其名义工资的购买力,如上所示。

p274.zh: 美国.最低工资和通货膨胀

p275.original: One sizable group of people has often received a large share of their income in a form that does not increase over time: retirees who receive a private company pension. Most pensions have traditionally been set as a fixed nominal dollar amount per year at retirement. For this reason, economists call pensions “defined benefits” plans. Even if inflation is low, the combination of inflation and a fixed income can create a substantial problem over time. A person who retires on a fixed income at age 65 will find that losing just 1% to 2% of buying power per year to inflation compounds to a considerable loss of buying power after a decade or two.
p275.zh: 相当一部分人往往以一段时间内不会增加的形式获得很大一部分收入:领取私营公司养恤金的退休人员。 大多数养恤金传统上定为每年退休时的固定名义美元数额。 为此,经济学家将养老金称为“确定的福利”计划。 即使通货膨胀率较低,通货膨胀和固定收入的结合也会随着时间的推移产生一个重大问题。65岁退休的固定收入者会发现,每年只有1%至2%的购买力被通货膨胀所抵消,在十年或两年后,购买力也大大下降。

p276.original: Fortunately, pensions and other defined benefits retirement plans are increasingly rare, replaced instead by “defined contribution” plans, such as 401(k)s and 403(b)s. In these plans, the employer contributes a fixed amount to the worker’s retirement account on a regular basis (usually every pay check). The employee often contributes as well. The worker invests these funds in a wide range of investment vehicles. These plans are tax deferred, and they are portable so that if the individual takes a job with a different employer, their 401(k) comes with them. To the extent that the investments made generate real rates of return, retirees are not burdened by the inflation costs of traditional pensioners.
p276.zh: 幸运的是,养恤金和其他确定福利的退休计划越来越少,取而代之的是401(k)和403(b)等“确定缴款”计划。 在这些计划中,雇主定期向工人的退休账户提供固定数额(通常是每次工资检查)。雇员也经常缴款。工人将这些资金投资于各种投资工具。 这些计划是推迟征税的,而且可以携带,这样,如果个人在不同的雇主那里工作,他们的401(k)就随他们一起来。 只要所作投资产生实际收益率,退休人员就不会受到传统养恤金领取人通货膨胀费用的负担。

p277.original: However, ordinary people can sometimes benefit from the unintended redistributions of inflation. Consider someone who borrows $10,000 to buy a car at a fixed interest rate of 9%. If inflation is 3% at the time the loan is made, then the borrower must repay the loan at a real interest rate of 6%. However, if inflation rises to 9%, then the real interest rate on the loan is zero. In this case, the borrower’s benefit from inflation is the lender’s loss. A borrower paying a fixed interest rate, who benefits from inflation, is just the flip side of an investor receiving a fixed interest rate, who suffers from inflation. The lesson is that when interest rates are fixed, rises in the rate of inflation tend to penalize suppliers of financial capital, who receive repayment in dollars that are worth less because of inflation, while demanders of financial capital end up better off, because they can repay their loans in dollars that are worth less than originally expected.
p277.zh: 然而,普通人有时可以从通货膨胀的意外再分配中受益。考虑借一万元的人,以9%的固定利率买车. 如果贷款时通货膨胀为3%,借款人必须按6%的实际利率偿还贷款。 然而,如果通货膨胀上升到9%,那么贷款的实际利率为零. 在这种情况下,借款人从通货膨胀中得益是贷款人的损失。支付固定利率的借款人从通货膨胀中受益,只是获得固定利率的投资者的反面,后者受到通货膨胀的影响.教训是,当利率固定下来时,通货膨胀率的上升往往会惩罚金融资本的提供者,后者因为通货膨胀而得到价值较低的美元偿还,而金融资本的需求者最终会好起来,因为他们能够以价值低于原先预期的美元偿还贷款.

p278.original: The unintended redistributions of buying power that inflation causes may have a broader effect on society. America’s widespread acceptance of market forces rests on a perception that people’s actions have a reasonable connection to market outcomes. When inflation causes a retiree who built up a pension or invested at a fixed interest rate to suffer, however, while someone who borrowed at a fixed interest rate benefits from inflation, it is hard to believe that this outcome was deserved in any way. Similarly, when homeowners benefit from inflation because the price of their homes rises, while renters suffer because they are paying higher rent, it is hard to see any useful incentive effects. One of the reasons that the general public dislikes inflation is a sense that it makes economic rewards and penalties more arbitrary—and therefore likely to be perceived as unfair – even dangerous, as the next Clear It Up feature shows.
p278.zh: 通货膨胀造成的购买力的意外再分配可能会对社会产生更广泛的影响。 美国广泛接受市场力量,是因为人们认为人民的行动与市场结果有合理联系。 然而,当通货膨胀导致退休者积聚养恤金或按固定利率投资时,当以固定利率借贷的人从通货膨胀中受益时,很难相信这种结果无论如何都是值得的。 同样,当房主由于住房价格上涨而受益于通货膨胀,而租房者由于支付较高的租金而蒙受损失时,很难看到任何有益的激励效应。公众不喜欢通货膨胀的原因之一是,它使经济奖惩更加武断,因此可能被视为不公平,甚至危险,下一个Clear It Up的特征就表明了这一点。

p279.original: Is there a connection between German hyperinflation and Hitler’s rise to power?
p279.zh: 德国恶性通货膨胀与希特勒上台有联系吗?

p280.original: Germany suffered an intense hyperinflation of its currency, the Mark, in the years after World War I, when the Weimar Republic in Germany resorted to printing money to pay its bills and the onset of the Great Depression created the social turmoil that Adolf Hitler was able to take advantage of in his rise to power. Shiller described the connection this way in a National Bureau of Economic Research 1996 Working Paper:
p280.zh: 德国在第一次世界大战之后的几年里,由于德国的魏玛共和国利用印钞来支付其帐单,而大萧条的开始,造成了阿道夫·希特勒在上台时能够利用的社会动荡.Shiller在1996年国家经济研究局的一份工作文件中说明了这种联系:

p281.original: A fact that is probably little known to young people today, even in Germany, is that the final collapse of the Mark in 1923, the time when the Mark’s inflation reached astronomical levels (inflation of 35,974.9% in November 1923 alone, for an annual rate that month of 4.69 × 1028%), came in the same month as did Hitler’s Beer Hall Putsch, his Nazi Party’s armed attempt to overthrow the German government. This failed putsch resulted in Hitler’s imprisonment, at which time he wrote his book Mein Kampf, setting forth an inspirational plan for Germany’s future, suggesting plans for world domination. . .
p281.zh: 即使是在德国,今天年轻人可能也鲜为人知的事实是马克号在1923年最终崩溃,当时马克号的通货膨胀达到了天文水平(仅1923年11月的通货膨胀率就达到35,974.9%,当月的年通货膨胀率为4.69×1028 %),而希特勒的啤酒厅普特希(Putsch)正是他纳粹党武装企图推翻德国政府的同期到来. 这一失败导致了希特勒的监禁,当时他写了他的书《Mein Kampf》,为德国的未来提出了鼓舞人心的计划,提出了统治世界的计划。

p282.original: . . . Most people in Germany today probably do not clearly remember these events; this lack of attention to it may be because its memory is blurred by the more dramatic events that succeeded it (the Nazi seizure of power and World War II). However, to someone living through these historical events in sequence . . . [the putsch] may have been remembered as vivid evidence of the potential effects of inflation.
p282.zh: . . ⁇ . 今天德国的大多数人可能没有清楚地记得这些事件;这种缺乏关注可能是因为其记忆被继承它的更戏剧性的事件(纳粹夺权事件和二战)所模糊. 然而,对于经历过这些历史事件的人来说,这些历史事件可能已被人们记住,作为通货膨胀潜在影响的生动证据。

p284.original: Prices are the messengers in a market economy, conveying information about conditions of demand and supply. Inflation blurs those price messages. Inflation means that we perceive price signals more vaguely, like a radio program received with considerable static. If the static becomes severe, it is hard to tell what is happening.
p284.zh: 价格是市场经济中的使者,传递关于供需状况的信息.通货膨胀模糊了这些价格信息。通货膨胀意味着,我们更模糊地看待价格信号,就像接收到相当静态的无线电节目一样。 如果静态变得严重,很难说出发生了什么。

p285.original: In Israel, when inflation accelerated to an annual rate of 500% in 1985, some stores stopped posting prices directly on items, since they would have had to put new labels on the items or shelves every few days to reflect inflation. Instead, a shopper just took items from a shelf and went up to the checkout register to find out the price for that day. Obviously, this situation makes comparing prices and shopping for the best deal rather difficult. When the levels and changes of prices become uncertain, businesses and individuals find it harder to react to economic signals. In a world where inflation is at a high rate, but bouncing up and down to some extent, does a higher price of a good mean that inflation has risen, or that supply of that good has decreased, or that demand for that good has increased? Should a buyer of the good take the higher prices as an economic hint to start substituting other products—or have the prices of the substitutes risen by an equal amount? Should a seller of the good take a higher price as a reason to increase production—or is the higher price only a sign of a general inflation in which the prices of all inputs to production are rising as well? The true story will presumably become clear over time, but at a given moment, who can say?
p285.zh: 在以色列,1985年通货膨胀加速到每年500%,一些商店停止直接对物品贴价,因为为了反映通货膨胀,它们不得不每隔几天在物品或货架上贴上新的标签。反之,一个垃圾桶从货架上拿走了物品,然后上到验票台,找出当天的价格. 显然,这种情况使得比较价格和购买最佳交易相当困难。 当价格水平和变化变得不确定时,企业和个人发现对经济信号的反应更加困难.在一个通货膨胀率很高但在一定程度上上下暴涨的世界中,高价的好价钱是否意味着通货膨胀上升,或者说这种商品的供应减少,或者对这种商品的需求增加?货物购买者应把较高的价格作为开始替代其他产品的经济暗示,还是代用品的价格要上涨同等数额?货物销售商是否应该以更高的价格作为增加生产的理由? 高价格是否只是普遍通货膨胀的征兆,其中所有生产投入的价格也在上升?真实的故事大概会随着时间而变得清晰,但在特定的时刻,谁能说出呢?

p286.original: High and variable inflation means that the incentives in the economy to adjust in response to changes in prices are weaker. Markets will adjust toward their equilibrium prices and quantities more erratically and slowly, and many individual markets will experience a greater chance of surpluses and shortages.
p286.zh: 高而可变的通货膨胀意味着经济中因应价格变化进行调整的动力较弱.市场将更不稳定、更缓慢地调整其平衡价格和数量,许多个别市场将面临更大的盈余和短缺机会。

p288.original: Inflation can make long-term planning difficult. In discussing unintended redistributions, we considered the case of someone trying to plan for retirement with a pension that is fixed in nominal terms and a high rate of inflation. Similar problems arise for all people trying to save for retirement, because they must consider what their money will really buy several decades in the future when we cannot know the rate of future inflation.
p288.zh: 通货膨胀可能使长期规划变得困难。 在讨论意外再分配时,我们考虑了有人试图计划退休的情况,其养恤金按名义条件固定,通货膨胀率很高。试图为退休储蓄的所有人也会出现类似问题,因为他们必须考虑,当我们不知道未来通货膨胀率时,他们的钱今后会真正买到什么。

p289.original: Inflation, especially at moderate or high levels, will pose substantial planning problems for businesses, too. A firm can make money from inflation—for example, by paying bills and wages as late as possible so that it can pay in inflated dollars, while collecting revenues as soon as possible. A firm can also suffer losses from inflation, as in the case of a retail business that gets stuck holding too much cash, only to see inflation eroding the value of that cash. However, when a business spends its time focusing on how to profit by inflation, or at least how to avoid suffering from it, an inevitable tradeoff strikes: less time is spent on improving products and services or on figuring out how to make existing products and services more cheaply. An economy with high inflation rewards businesses that have found clever ways of profiting from inflation, which are not necessarily the businesses that excel at productivity, innovation, or quality of service.
p289.zh: 通货膨胀,特别是中等或高水平的通货膨胀,也会给企业带来重大的规划问题。公司可以通过通货膨胀赚钱——例如,通过支付账单和工资尽可能晚,从而能够以夸大美元支付,同时尽快收取收入。公司也可能因通货膨胀而蒙受损失,例如,一个被卡住持有过多现金的零售企业,只能看到通货膨胀侵蚀了该现金的价值。 然而,当一个企业花时间专注于如何通过通货膨胀获利,或者至少如何避免遭受通货膨胀的伤害时,必然会发生权衡:在改善产品和服务或想出如何使现有产品和服务更便宜方面花费的时间较少。高通胀率的经济奖励了那些已经找到从通货膨胀中获利的巧妙方法的企业,而通货膨胀不一定是那些在生产力、创新或服务质量方面表现优异的企业。

p290.original: In the short term, low or moderate levels of inflation may not pose an overwhelming difficulty for business planning, because costs of doing business and sales revenues may rise at similar rates. If, however, inflation varies substantially over the short or medium term, then it may make sense for businesses to stick to shorter-term strategies. The evidence as to whether relatively low rates of inflation reduce productivity is controversial among economists. There is some evidence that if inflation can be held to moderate levels of less than 3% per year, it need not prevent a nation’s real economy from growing at a healthy pace. For some countries that have experienced hyperinflation of several thousand percent per year, an annual inflation rate of 20–30% may feel basically the same as zero. However, several economists have pointed to the suggestive fact that when U.S. inflation heated up in the early 1970s—to 10%—U.S. growth in productivity slowed down, and when inflation slowed down in the 1980s, productivity edged up again not long thereafter, as  shows.
p290.zh: 从短期来看,低或中度的通货膨胀可能不会给业务规划带来压倒性的困难,因为做生意的成本和销售收入可能会以类似的速度上升。 但是,如果短期或中期的通货膨胀差别很大,那么,企业坚持短期战略也许有道理。相对较低的通货膨胀率是否降低生产率的证据在经济学家中引起争议.有一些证据表明,如果通货膨胀能够维持在每年不到3%的温和水平上,那么它就不必阻止一个国家实体经济的健康增长。 对于一些年均恶性通货膨胀达几千 %的国家来说,年通货膨胀率为20-30%可能感觉基本与零相同。 然而,一些经济学家指出,一个令人暗示的事实,即美国通货膨胀在1970年代早期升温时——美国生产率增长放缓至10-%,1980年代通货膨胀放缓时,生产率在此后不久再次攀升,如前所述。

p291.original: U.S. Inflation Rate and U.S. Labor Productivity, 1961–2020
p291.zh: 美国.通货膨胀率和美国.1961-2020年劳动生产率

p292.zh: 通货膨胀有什么好处吗?

p293.original: Although the economic effects of inflation are primarily negative, two countervailing points are worth noting. First, the impact of inflation will differ considerably according to whether it is creeping up slowly at 0% to 2% per year, galloping along at 10% to 20% per year, or racing to the point of hyperinflation at, say, 40% per month. Hyperinflation can rip an economy and a society apart. An annual inflation rate of 2%, 3%, or 4%, however, is a long way from a national crisis. Low inflation is also better than deflation which occurs with severe recessions.
p293.zh: 虽然通货膨胀的经济影响主要是负面的,但有两个反补贴点值得注意。 首先,通货膨胀的影响将有很大的不同,这取决于它是否缓慢地以每年0到2 %的速度上升,每年以10到20 %的速度上升,还是以每月40%的速度达到恶性通货膨胀的程度。高通胀会把经济与社会撕裂。 然而,年通货膨胀率为2%、3%或4%,远离国家危机。低通货膨胀也优于严重衰退时出现的通货紧缩。

p294.original: Second, economists sometimes argue that moderate inflation may help the economy by making wages in labor markets more flexible. The discussion in Unemployment pointed out that wages tend to be sticky in their downward movements and that unemployment can result. A little inflation could nibble away at real wages, and thus help real wages to decline if necessary. In this way, even if a moderate or high rate of inflation may act as sand in the gears of the economy, perhaps a low rate of inflation serves as oil for the gears of the labor market. This argument is controversial. A full analysis would have to account for all the effects of inflation. It does, however, offer another reason to believe that, all things considered, very low rates of inflation may not be especially harmful.
p294.zh: 第二,经济学家有时认为,温和的通货膨胀可能通过使劳动力市场的工资更加灵活而帮助经济。" 失业 " 的讨论指出,工资在向下流动时往往很粘滞,因此,失业是可能造成的。微弱的通货膨胀可能会使实际工资下降,从而帮助实际工资在必要情况下下降。 这样,即使中度或高通胀率可能在经济工具中起到沙子的作用,但低通胀率也许可作为劳动力市场工具的石油。 这一论点引起争议.全面分析必须说明通货膨胀的所有影响。 然而,它确实提供了另一个理由,可以认为,无论什么因素,非常低的通货膨胀率可能不会特别有害。

p296.original: Unexpected inflation will tend to hurt those whose money received, in terms of wages and interest payments, does not rise with inflation. In contrast, inflation can help those who owe money that they can pay in less valuable, inflated dollars. Low rates of inflation have relatively little economic impact over the short term. Over the medium and the long term, even low rates of inflation can complicate future planning. High rates of inflation can muddle price signals in the short term and prevent market forces from operating efficiently, and can vastly complicate long-term savings and investment decisions.
p296.zh: 意外的通货膨胀往往会伤害那些从工资和利息支付方面收到的资金不会随着通货膨胀而增加的人。与此相反,通货膨胀可以帮助那些欠钱的人,他们能够用价值较低、夸大美元支付这些钱。短期内,低通货膨胀率对经济的影响相对较小。 从中长期来看,即使低通货膨胀率也可能使今后的规划复杂化。高通货膨胀率可以在短期内搅乱价格信号,使市场力量无法有效运作,并会使长期储蓄和投资决定大为复杂化。

p298.original: If inflation rises unexpectedly by 5%, would a state government that had recently borrowed money to pay for a new highway benefit or lose?
p298.zh: 如果通货膨胀出乎意料地上升5%,那么最近借钱支付新高速公路福利的州政府会否输?

p299.original: The state government would benefit because it would repay the loan in less valuable dollars than it borrowed. Plus, tax revenues for the state government would increase because of the inflation.
p299.zh: 州政府将受益,因为它将用比所借价值低的美元偿还贷款. 此外,由于通货膨胀,州政府的税收将增加。

p301.original: Identify several parties likely to be helped and hurt by inflation.
p301.zh: 查明几个可能因通货膨胀而受帮助和伤害的当事方。

p303.original: If, over time, wages and salaries on average rise at least as fast as inflation, why do people worry about how inflation affects incomes?
p303.zh: 如果随着时间的推移,平均工资和薪金的上涨至少与通货膨胀一样快,人们为什么担心通货膨胀如何影响收入?

p304.original: Who in an economy is the big winner from inflation?
p304.zh: 在经济中,谁是通货膨胀的大赢家?

p306.original: Shiller, Robert. “Why Do People Dislike Inflation?” NBER Working Paper Series, National Bureau of Economic Research, p. 52. 1996.
p306.zh: (原始内容存档于2018-03-27). Shiller, Robert.“为什么人们不喜欢通货膨胀?”52. 国家1996 (英语).

p308.original: When a price, wage, or interest rate is adjusted automatically with inflation, economists use the term indexed. An indexed payment increases according to the index number that measures inflation. Those in private markets and government programs observe a wide range of indexing arrangements. Since the negative effects of inflation depend in large part on having inflation unexpectedly affect one part of the economy but not another—say, increasing the prices that people pay but not the wages that workers receive—indexing will take some of the sting out of inflation.
p308.zh: 当某一价格,工资,或利率随通货膨胀而自动调整时,经济学家会使用指数化的术语.指数化的付款额根据衡量通货膨胀的指数增加。私营市场和政府方案中的指数化安排范围很广。 由于通货膨胀的负面影响很大程度上取决于通货膨胀意外地影响到经济的一个部分,而不是另一个部分,也就是说,提高人们支付的价格,而不是工人得到的工资,指数化将使通货膨胀产生一些影响。

p310.original: In the 1970s and 1980s, labor unions commonly negotiated wage contracts that had cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) which guaranteed that their wages would keep up with inflation. These contracts were sometimes written as, for example, COLA plus 3%. Thus, if inflation was 5%, the wage increase would automatically be 8%, but if inflation rose to 9%, the wage increase would automatically be 12%. COLAs are a form of indexing applied to wages.
p310.zh: 在1970年代和1980年代,工会通常谈判工资合同,这些合同规定了生活费调整,保证其工资与通货膨胀保持同步。 这些合同有时写成COLA加3%。 因此,如果通货膨胀为5%,工资将自动增加8%,但如果通货膨胀上升到9%,工资将自动增加12%。工资指数是一种适用于工资的指数化形式。

p311.original: Loans often have built-in inflation adjustments, too, so that if the inflation rate rises by two percentage points, then the interest rate that a financial institution charges on the loan rises by two percentage points as well. An adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) is a type of loan that one can use to purchase a home in which the interest rate varies with the rate of inflation. Often, a borrower will be able to receive a lower interest rate if borrowing with an ARM, compared to a fixed-rate loan. The reason is that with an ARM, the lender is protected against the risk that higher inflation will reduce the real loan payments, and so the risk premium part of the interest rate can be correspondingly lower.
p311.zh: 贷款也经常有内在的通货膨胀调整,因此,如果通货膨胀率上升两个百分点,那么金融机构对贷款收取的利率也上升两个百分点。 可调整利率的抵押贷款(ARM)是一种可以用来购买住房的贷款,其中利率随通货膨胀率而变化。借款人通常能够与固定利率贷款相比,通过ARM借贷获得较低的利率。原因是,如果贷款人持有ARM,那么贷款人就受到保护,免受通货膨胀上升会减少实际贷款支付的风险,因此利率的风险溢价部分可以相应降低.

p312.original: A number of ongoing or long-term business contracts also have provisions that prices will adjust automatically according to inflation. Sellers like such contracts because they are not locked into a low nominal selling price if inflation turns out higher than expected. Buyers like such contracts because they are not locked into a high buying price if inflation turns out to be lower than expected. A contract with automatic adjustments for inflation in effect agrees on a real price for the borrower to pay, rather than a nominal price.
p312.zh: 一些进行中或长期的业务合同也有规定,价格将根据通货膨胀自动调整。销售商喜欢这种合同,因为如果通货膨胀高于预期,它们不会陷入低名义销售价格。买方喜欢这种合同,因为如果通货膨胀低于预期,他们不会陷入高价购买。一项对通货膨胀进行自动调整的合同实际上同意借款人支付的实际价格,而不是名义价格。

p314.original: Many government programs are indexed to inflation. The U.S. income tax code is designed so that as a person’s income rises above certain levels, the tax rate on the marginal income earned rises as well. That is what the expression “move into a higher tax bracket” means. For example, according to the basic tax tables from the Internal Revenue Service, in 2020, a married person filing jointly owed 10% of all taxable income from $0 to $19,750; 12% of all income from $19,751 to $80,250; 22% of all taxable income from $80,251 to $171,050; 24% of all taxable income from $171,051 to $326,600; 32% of all taxable income from $326,601 to $414,700; 35% of all taxable income from $414,701 to $622,050; and 37% of all income from $622,051 and above.
p314.zh: 许多政府方案都与通货膨胀挂钩。 美国所得税法的设计是为了让一个人的收入超过一定水平,边际所得的税率也随之上升. 这就是“转入更高税率”的含义。 例如,根据国内税务局的基本税务表,2020年,已婚者共同欠缴所有应纳税所得额的10%,即从0美元到19 750美元;19 751美元到80 250美元所有应纳税所得额的12%;80 251美元到171 050美元所有应纳税所得额的22%;171 051美元到326 600美元所有应纳税所得额的24%;326 601美元到414 700美元所有应纳税所得额的32%;414 701美元到622 050美元所有应纳税所得额的35%;622 051美元及以上所有应纳税所得额的37%。

p315.original: Because of the many complex provisions in the rest of the tax code, it is difficult to determine exactly the taxes an individual owes the government based on these numbers, but the numbers illustrate the basic theme that tax rates rise as the marginal dollar of income rises. Until the late 1970s, if nominal wages increased along with inflation, people were moved into higher tax brackets and owed a higher proportion of their income in taxes, even though their real income had not risen. In 1981, the government eliminated this “bracket creep”. Now, the income levels where higher tax rates kick in are indexed to rise automatically with inflation.
p315.zh: 由于税法其他部分有许多复杂的规定,因此很难根据这些数字确切确定个人应向政府缴纳的税费,但这些数字说明了随着收入的边际美元增加而税率上升的基本主题. 直到20世纪70年代末,如果名义工资随通货膨胀而增加,人们被转移到更高的税额中,并欠下较高比例的收入的税收,尽管他们的实际收入没有上升.1981年,政府消除了这种“裂缝爬行动物”。 现在,高税率触发的收入水平随着通货膨胀而自动上升。

p316.original: The Social Security program offers two examples of indexing. Since the passage of the Social Security Indexing Act of 1972, the level of Social Security benefits increases each year along with the Consumer Price Index. Also, Social Security is funded by payroll taxes, which the government imposes on the income earned up to a certain amount—$137,700 in 2020. The government adjusts this level of income upward each year according to the rate of inflation, so that an indexed increase in the Social Security tax base accompanies the indexed rise in the benefit level.
p316.zh: 社会保障方案提供了两个指数化的例子。 自1972年《社会保障指数法》通过以来,社会保障福利水平每年随消费物价指数而增加。 另外,社会保障由工资税供资,政府对收入征收工资税,到2020年达到一定数额——137,700美元。 政府每年根据通货膨胀率向上调整这一收入水平,使社会保障税基指数化增长与指数化增长的福利水平相伴随。

p317.original: As yet another example of a government program affected by indexing, in 1996 the U.S., government began offering indexed bonds. Bonds are means by which the U.S. government (and many private-sector companies as well) borrows money; that is, investors buy the bonds, and then the government repays the money with interest. Traditionally, government bonds have paid a fixed rate of interest. This policy gave a government that had borrowed an incentive to encourage inflation, because it could then repay its past borrowing in inflated dollars at a lower real interest rate. However, indexed bonds promise to pay a certain real rate of interest above whatever inflation rate occurs. In the case of a retiree trying to plan for the long term and worried about the risk of inflation, for example, indexed bonds that guarantee a rate of return higher than inflation—no matter the level of inflation—can be a very comforting investment.
p317.zh: 作为受指数化影响的政府方案的另一个例子,美国于1996年开始提供指数化债券.债券是美国政府(以及许多私营部门公司)借钱的手段;即投资者购买债券,然后政府用利息偿还这笔钱.传统上,政府债券支付固定利率.这项政策使一个政府借钱鼓励通货膨胀,因为这样它就可以以较低的实际利率偿还过去高涨的美元借款。 然而,指数化的债券承诺支付一定的实际利率,高于任何通货膨胀率。 如果退休人员试图长期计划,并担心通货膨胀的风险,例如,保证回报率高于通货膨胀率的指数化债券——无论通货膨胀水平如何——都可能是一种非常令人欣慰的投资。

p318.original: Might Indexing Reduce Concern over Inflation?
p318.zh: 能否将降低对通货膨胀的关注指数化?

p319.original: Indexing may seem like an obviously useful step. After all, when individuals, firms, and government programs are indexed against inflation, then people can worry less about arbitrary redistributions and other effects of inflation.
p319.zh: 索引编制似乎显然是有益的一步。毕竟,当个人、企业和政府计划被指数化以抵御通货膨胀时,人们可以减少对任意再分配和通货膨胀的其他影响的担忧。

p320.original: However, some of the fiercest opponents of inflation express grave concern about indexing. They point out that indexing is always partial. Not every employer will provide COLAs for workers. Not all companies can assume that costs and revenues will rise in lockstep with the general rates of inflation. Not all interest rates for borrowers and savers will change to match inflation exactly. However, as partial inflation indexing spreads, the political opposition to inflation may diminish. After all, older people whose Social Security benefits are protected against inflation, or banks that have loaned their money with adjustable-rate loans, no longer have as much reason to care whether inflation heats up. In a world where some people are indexed against inflation and some are not, financially savvy businesses and investors may seek out ways to be protected against inflation, while the financially unsophisticated and small businesses may feel it the most.
p320.zh: 然而,一些最强烈的通货膨胀反对者对指数化表示严重关切. 他们指出,索引总是部分的。并不是每个雇主都为工人提供职业资格证书。并非所有公司都能假定成本和收入会随着总的通货膨胀率而上升。并非所有借款人和储蓄者的利率都会发生与通货膨胀完全相符的变化。 然而,随着部分通货膨胀指数的扩大,对通货膨胀的政治反对可能会减少。毕竟,社会保障福利受到保护的老年人,或者用可调整利率贷款的银行,不再有同样的理由去关心通货膨胀是否加剧。在一个一些人受通货膨胀影响而有些人则没有指数的世界中,在财政上富于活力的企业和投资者可能寻求防止通货膨胀的方法,而财政上不成熟的小企业则可能感到最强烈。

p321.original: A Preview of Policy Discussions of Inflation
p321.zh: 通货膨胀政策讨论预览

p322.original: This chapter has focused on how economists measure inflation, historical experience with inflation, how to adjust nominal variables into real ones, how inflation affects the economy, and how indexing works. We have barely hinted at the causes of inflation, and we have not addressed government policies to deal with inflation. We will examine these issues in depth in other chapters. However, it is useful to offer a preview here.
p322.zh: 本章主要论述经济学家如何衡量通货膨胀,通货膨胀的历史经验,如何将名义变量调整为实际变量,通货膨胀如何影响经济,以及指数化如何发挥作用等问题. 我们几乎没有暗示通货膨胀的原因,我们也没有针对政府政策来应对通货膨胀。 我们将在其他章节中深入探讨这些问题。 不过,在此提供预览是有用的。

p323.original: We can sum up the cause of inflation in one phrase: Too many dollars chasing too few goods. The great surges of inflation early in the twentieth century came after wars, which are a time when government spending is very high, but consumers have little to buy, because production is going to the war effort. Governments also commonly impose price controls during wartime. After the war, the price controls end and pent-up buying power surges forth, driving up inflation. Otherwise, if too few dollars are chasing too many goods, then inflation will decline or even turn into deflation. Therefore, we typically associate slowdowns in economic activity, as in major recessions and the Great Depression, with a reduction in inflation or even outright deflation.
p323.zh: 我们可以用一句话来概括通货膨胀的原因:太多的美元追逐太少的商品.20世纪早期通货膨胀的猛增是战后发生的,当时政府开支非常高,但消费者买不起,因为生产要投入战争努力. 各国政府在战争期间也通常实行价格管制。战后,价格控制结束,倒数购买力激增,导致通货膨胀上升. 否则,如果太少的美元追逐太多的货物,通货膨胀就会下降甚至变成通货紧缩. 因此,我们通常将经济活动放缓,如大衰退和大萧条,与通货膨胀下降甚至完全通货紧缩联系起来。

p324.original: The policy implications are clear. If we are to avoid inflation, the amount of purchasing power in the economy must grow at roughly the same rate as the production of goods. Macroeconomic policies that the government can use to affect the amount of purchasing power—through taxes, spending, and regulation of interest rates and credit—can thus cause inflation to rise or reduce inflation to lower levels.
p324.zh: 政策影响是明确的。 如果我们要避免通货膨胀,经济的购买力就必须以与商品生产大致相同的速度增长. 因此,政府可以用来影响购买力的宏观经济政策——通过税收、支出和利率及信贷的调节——可导致通货膨胀上升或降低到较低的水平。

p325.original: Inflation in a Pandemic—A Return to the 1970s, or a Temporary Adjustment?
p325.zh: 通货膨胀在大流行中 -- -- 回到1970年代,还是暂时调整?

p326.original: The pandemic-induced recession caused all sorts of disruptions to our economy, including inflation. During the pandemic, the prices for goods like gas and cars fell as people shifted to remote work and canceled travel plans. But as the economy started to recover from the pandemic in early 2021, we started to see large increases in these prices. Higher prices were also fueled by the injections of cash into the economy through stimulus checks and unemployment benefits. The pandemic also caused shortages throughout the global supply chain, further pushing prices up (you'll learn more about this idea in a few chapters when we talk about aggregate supply and demand).
p326.zh: 大流行病引起的衰退对我国经济造成各种破坏,包括通货膨胀。 在这场大流行期间,由于人们转向远程工作,取消了旅行计划,天然气和汽车等商品的价格下跌。 但随着经济在2021年初开始从这场大流行中复苏,我们开始看到这些价格的大幅上涨. 通过刺激检查和失业福利向经济注入现金,也助长了价格上涨。 这个流行病也造成了全球供应链的短缺,进一步推高了价格(当我们谈论总供求时,你会在几章中更多地了解这个想法)。

p327.original: With headline annualized inflation rates in 2021 exceeding 6%, the question in the next few years is whether we'll see permanently high inflation rates of 9%, 10%, or more, like we did in the 1970s and early-1980s. Some economists believe the pandemic-induced inflation is just a transitory adjustment—indeed, used car and gasoline prices rose dramatically in 2010 and 2011 as well, as we were recovering from the Great Recession. Others are more concerned that the inflation is permanent. Shortages continue to exist throughout the economy as of early 2022, and if consumers expect higher inflation, it can be a self-fulfilling prophecy, as they start buying things now in order to avoid future bouts of inflation.
p327.zh: 随着2021年头条年化通货膨胀率超过6%,接下来几年的问题就是,我们是否会像20世纪70年代和80年代初那样,看到9%,10%,甚至更高的永久性高通货膨胀率. 一些经济学家认为,大流行引发的通货膨胀只是暂时性的调整 — — 事实上,废旧汽车和汽油价格在2010年和2011年也大幅上涨,因为我们正在从大衰退中复苏。其他人则更担心通货膨胀是永久性的。 从2022年初起,整个经济中仍然存在着短缺,如果消费者期望更高的通胀率,那就可能是一个自我实现的预言,因为他们现在开始买东西,以避免未来通货膨胀的暴涨.

p328.original: As you learned about earlier, inflation is a major concern of consumers, if less of an issue among economists. But inflation should be matched by increases in living standards, otherwise there could be major implications for the economy.
p328.zh: 正如你之前所了解的,通货膨胀是消费者的主要关切, 经济学家中的问题就更少了。 但是,通货膨胀应当与生活水平的提高相匹配,否则将对经济产生重大影响。

p330.original: A payment is indexed if it is automatically adjusted for inflation. Examples of indexing in the private sector include wage contracts with cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) and loan agreements like adjustable-rate mortgages (ARMs). Examples of indexing in the public sector include tax brackets and Social Security payments.
p330.zh: 付款如果根据通货膨胀自动调整,则指数化。私营部门指数化的例子包括有生活费调整的工资合同和可调整利率抵押贷款等贷款协议。公共部门的指数化例子包括税额和社会保障付款。

p332.original: How should an increase in inflation affect the interest rate on an adjustable-rate mortgage?
p332.zh: 通货膨胀的上升应如何影响可调整利率的抵押贷款利率?

p333.original: Higher inflation reduces real interest rates on fixed rate mortgages. Because ARMs can be adjusted, higher inflation leads to higher interest rates on ARMs.
p333.zh: 较高的通货膨胀降低了固定利率抵押贷款的实际利率。 由于ARM可以调整,较高的通货膨胀导致ARM的利率较高.

p334.original: A fixed-rate mortgage has the same interest rate over the life of the loan, whether the mortgage is for 15 or 30 years. By contrast, an adjustable-rate mortgage changes with market interest rates over the life of the mortgage. If inflation falls unexpectedly by 3%, what would likely happen to a homeowner with an adjustable-rate mortgage?
p334.zh: 固定利率的抵押贷款在贷款存续期内,无论抵押贷款期限为15年还是30年,其利率相同.相比之下,可调整利率的抵押在整个抵押期随市场利率的变化而变化。 如果通货膨胀意外下降3%,那么拥有可调整利率的抵押贷款的房主将会发生什么?

p335.original: Because the mortgage has an adjustable rate, the rate should fall by 3%, the same as inflation, to keep the real interest rate the same.
p335.zh: 由于抵押贷款有可调整的利率,利率应该下降3%,与通货膨胀相同,以保持实际利率不变.

p338.original: Name several forms of indexing in the private and public sector.
p338.zh: 列举私营和公共部门的几种指数化形式。

p340.original: If a government gains from unexpected inflation when it borrows, why would it choose to offer indexed bonds?
p340.zh: 如果政府借债时意外通货膨胀得益,为什么它会选择提供指数化的债券?

p341.original: Do you think perfect indexing is possible? Why or why not?
p341.zh: 你认为完美索引是可能的吗? 为什么或为什么不呢?

A union member with a COLA wage contract
Someone with a large stash of cash in a safe deposit box
A bank lending money at a fixed rate of interest
A person who is not due to receive a pay raise for another 11 months

p344.original: Rosalie the Retiree knows that when she retires in 16 years, her company will give her a one-time payment of $20,000. However, if the inflation rate is 6% per year, how much buying power will that $20,000 have when measured in today’s dollars? Hint: Start by calculating the rise in the price level over the 16 years.
p344.zh: 罗莎莉退休后知道她16年后退休后,她的公司会给她一次性支付2万美元. 然而,如果通货膨胀率是每年6%,那么以今天的美元衡量的20 000美元的购买力会有多大?提示:从计算16年来物价水平的上涨开始.

c3.original: Graph a shows the trends in the U.S. price level from the year 1947 to 2020. In 1947, the graph starts out close to 22. It gradually increases until about 1973, then increases more rapidly through the remainder of the 1970s and beyond, with periodic dips, until 2020, when it  reached around 260. Graph b shows the trends in U.S. inflation rates from the year 1948 to 2020. In 1948, the graph starts out with inflation at almost 7%, goes up and down periodically, with peaks in the 1940s and the 1970s, until settling to around 1.2% in 2020.
c3.zh: 图a显示了1947年至2020年美国价格水平的趋势。1947年,该图开始近22. 它逐渐增加,直到大约1973年,然后在1970年代余下时间和以后更迅速地增加,有周期性地增加,直到2020年达到260年左右. 图b显示1948年至2020年美国通货膨胀率的趋势。1948年,该图以通货膨胀率近7%为起点,定期上下波动,20世纪40年代和70年代达到峰值,直到2020年稳定在1.2%左右.

c6.original: After adjusting for inflation, the federal minimum wage dropped about 30 percent from 1965–2020, even though the nominal figure climbed from $1.40 to $7.25 per hour. Increases in the minimum wage in between 2008 and 2010 kept the decline from being worse—as it would have been if the wage had remained the same as it did from 1997 through 2007. Since 2010, the real minimum wage has continued to decline. (Sources: http://www.dol.gov/whd/minwage/chart.htm and http://data.bls.gov/cgi-bin/surveymost?cu)
c6.zh: 在根据通货膨胀作出调整后,联邦最低工资从1965-2020年下降了约30%,尽管名义上的数字从每小时1.40美元上升到7.25美元。2008至2010年最低工资的提高使这一下降不会恶化——如果工资与1997至2007年一样的话。 自2010年以来,实际最低工资持续下降。(资料来源:http://www.dol.gov/whd/minwage/chart.htm和http://data.bls.gov/cgi-bin/surveymost?cu) 互联网档案馆的存檔,存档日期2013-03-02.

c7.original: Over the last several decades in the United States, there have been times when rising inflation rates have been closely followed by lower productivity rates and lower inflation rates have corresponded to increasing productivity rates. As the graph shows, however, this correlation does not always exist.
c7.zh: 在过去几十年中,美国的通货膨胀率不断上升,紧随其后的是生产率的降低,通货膨胀率的降低也与生产率的提高相对应。 然而,如图所示,这种相关性并非始终存在。
